title.raw: 卷107下 律曆志三下 Volume 107b Treatise 3: Treatise on Music and Calendars 2

sentences.zh: 自天地剖判，日月運行，剛柔相摩，寒暑交謝，分之以氣序，紀之以星辰，弦望有盈缺，明晦有修短。

translations.literal: From when Heaven and Earth were first divided, the sun and moon have run their courses; hard and soft grind against each other; cold and heat take turns in departing; they are distinguished by the sequence of qi, recorded by the stars; waxing and waning have fullness and lack, brightness and darkness have length and brevity.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Heaven and Earth were sundered, the sun and moon have pursued their circuits, yin and yang rubbing against each other as cold and warmth succeed one another. The seasons are ordered by the flow of qi, the heavens marked by the stars; the moon's phases wax and wane, and light and dark each have their measure.

sentences.zh: 古先哲王則之成化，迎日推策，各有司存，以天下之至王，盡生民之能事，先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時。

translations.literal: The sage kings of antiquity took this as their model to complete transformation, welcoming the sun and pushing the counting rods, each having its office; with the paramount kingship under Heaven, they exhausted what the people could do; anticipating Heaven, Heaven did not contradict them; following Heaven afterward, they received Heaven's seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The sage rulers of old modeled themselves on these patterns to bring civilization to fulfillment. They greeted the sun and advanced the reckoning, each duty assigned to its officer. As kings paramount under Heaven, they brought all that the people could accomplish to bear—acting before Heaven so that Heaven did not thwart them, and acting after Heaven so that they accorded with its seasons.

sentences.zh: 及卯金受命，年曆屢改，當塗啟運，日官變業，分路揚鑣，異門馳騖，回互靡定，交錯不等。

translations.literal: When the Mao-metal received the Mandate, the year-calendar was changed repeatedly; when the road of yellow earth opened its fortune, the officers of the day changed their profession; they split ways and waved their whips, raced in different gates, turning and crossing without fixity, interweaving unequally.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty received the Mandate, calendrical systems were revised again and again. When the Wei rose to power, the official astronomers changed their methods. Calendrical schools went their separate ways, each pursuing its own course, so that systems overlapped and conflicted without ever settling into agreement.

sentences.zh: 豈是人情淺深，苟相違異？

translations.literal: How could it be the shallowness or depth of human feeling, casually differing from each other?
translations.idiomatic: Surely this was not merely a matter of human prejudice, with scholars capriciously disagreeing?

sentences.zh: 蓋亦天道盈縮，欲止不能。

translations.literal: It is rather that the Way of Heaven has fullness and contraction, wishing to stop but unable.
translations.idiomatic: Rather, it reflected the waxing and waning of the Heavenly Way—one might wish to halt the process, but could not.

sentences.zh: 正光之曆既行於世，發元壬子，置差令朔。

translations.literal: Once the Zhengguang calendar had been put into use in the world, it took the origin in the renzi year and set discrepancies to align the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhengguang calendar came into use, with its epoch set in a renzi year, it adjusted discrepancies to fix the new moons.

sentences.zh: [1]測影清臺，懸炭之期或爽；

translations.literal: [1] On the Clear Terrace for measuring shadows, the period of the suspended charcoal sometimes missed;
translations.idiomatic: [1] On the Clear Terrace where shadows were measured, the timing of the suspended-charcoal test sometimes proved off;

sentences.zh: 候氣重室，布灰之應少差。

translations.literal: in the layered chamber for observing qi, the response of the spread ash showed slight discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: and in the sealed chamber where seasonal qi was observed, the ash-line responses showed small errors.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下當璧膺符，大橫恊兆，乘機虎變，撫運龍飛，苞括九隅，牢籠萬宇，四海來王，百靈受職。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that Your Majesty, bearing the jade disk and receiving the talisman, the great crossbeam harmonizing the omen, seizing the moment like a tiger's transformation, nurturing fortune like a dragon's ascent, embracing the nine corners, enclosing the myriad realms, the four seas coming as kings, the hundred spirits receiving their offices.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly observe that Your Majesty has received the Mandate, the great portent aligning with Heaven's signs; rising with the tiger's swift transformation and ascending with the dragon's flight, you encompass the farthest reaches and hold all under Heaven within your grasp, so that the four seas pay homage and the myriad spirits take their appointed places.

sentences.zh: 大丞相、勃海王降神挺生，固天縱德，負圖作宰，知機成務，撥亂反正，決江疏河，效顯勤王，勳彰濟世。

translations.literal: The Grand Chancellor, Prince of Bohai, descended spirit and stood forth born, firmly Heaven-endowed in virtue, bearing the chart as chief minister, knowing the moment and completing affairs, setting right disorder and restoring the correct, cutting through rivers and dredging streams, his merit displayed in serving the king, his achievement manifest in aiding the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Chancellor, Prince of Bohai, was born of Heaven's grace, endowed with virtue by nature. Bearing the cosmic chart as chief minister, he seized the opportune moment and accomplished great tasks—quelling disorder, restoring order, cutting through rivers and opening waterways—his loyalty to the throne and his service to the age shining forth in equal measure.

sentences.zh: 功成治定，禮樂惟新，以履端歸餘，術數未盡，乃命兼散騎常侍執讀臣李業興，大丞相府東閤祭酒、夷安縣開國公臣王春，大丞相府戶曹參軍臣和貴興等，委其刊正。

translations.literal: When achievement was complete and order settled, rites and music were renewed; because the beginning of the year and the return of surplus in calendrical reckoning were not yet exhausted, he then ordered the concurrent Regular Attendant Reader Li Yexing, the Grand Chancellor's Eastern Pavilion Libationer and Duke of Yi'an Wang Chun, the Grand Chancellor's Household Section Staff Member He Guixing, and others, entrusting them with revision and correction.
translations.idiomatic: Once success was won and order restored, rites and music were renewed; yet the calendrical reckoning of year-beginnings and intercalary remainders was still incomplete. The Emperor therefore commissioned Li Yexing, Reader-in-Attendance, Wang Chun, Libationer of the Grand Chancellor's Eastern Pavilion and Duke of Yi'an, He Guixing of the Household Section, and others to revise and correct the calendar.

sentences.zh: 但回舍有疾徐，推步有疏密，不可以一方知，難得以一途揆。

translations.literal: But circuit-return and lodge have fast and slow; pushing steps have sparse and dense; one cannot know from a single direction, nor easily gauge by a single path.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the cycles of lodge-return vary in speed, and computational steps differ in density; no single method can grasp the whole, nor can one pathway alone serve to judge them.

sentences.zh: 大丞相主簿臣孫搴，驃騎將軍、左光祿大夫臣曄，前給事黃門侍郎臣季景，勃海王世子開府諮議參軍事、定州大中正臣崔暹，業興息國子學生、屯留縣開國子臣子述等，並令參豫，定其是非。

translations.literal: The Grand Chancellor's Registrar Sun Qian, the General of Agile Cavalry and Left Household Gentleman of the Luminous Hall Ye, the former Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Ji Jing, the Bohai Heir Apparent's Staff Consultant for the Opening Office and Chief Rectifier of Ding Province Cui Xian, Li Yexing's son the Imperial University student and Baron of Tunliu Zi Shu, and others were all ordered to participate and decide what was right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qian, Registrar to the Grand Chancellor; Ye, General of Agile Cavalry and Left Household Gentleman of the Luminous Hall; Ji Jing, former Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; Cui Xian, Consultant of the Bohai Heir Apparent's staff and Chief Rectifier of Ding Province; Zi Shu, son of Li Yexing, Imperial University student and Baron of Tunliu—all were ordered to take part and adjudicate the merits of the calendar.

sentences.zh: 臣等職司其憂，猶恐未盡。

translations.literal: We, your ministers, in office bear this concern, yet still fear it is not complete.
translations.idiomatic: We who hold this office bear the responsibility, yet still fear our efforts may fall short.

sentences.zh: 竊以蒙戎為飾，必藉眾腋之華；

translations.literal: We venture to think that to adorn with fox-fur, one must rely on the splendor of many armpits;
translations.idiomatic: We venture to think that a fur cloak cannot be made from a single patch of hide;

sentences.zh: 輪奐成宇，寧止一枝之用。

translations.literal: to complete a hall with splendor, how could one branch alone suffice.
translations.idiomatic: nor can a great hall be built from a single rafter alone.

sentences.zh: 必集名勝，更共修理。

translations.literal: One must gather renowned experts to revise and repair it together.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned experts must be gathered to revise the work together.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫臣盧道約，大司農卿、彭城侯臣李諧，左光祿大夫、東雍州大中正臣裴獻伯，散騎常侍、西兗州大中正臣溫子昇，太尉府長史臣陸操，尚書右丞、城陽縣開國子臣盧元明，中書侍郎臣李同軌，前中書侍郎臣邢子明，中書侍郎臣宇文忠之，前司空府長史、建康伯臣元仲悛，大丞相法曹參軍臣杜弼，尚書左中兵郎中、定陽伯臣李溥濟，尚書起部郎中臣辛術，尚書祠部郎中臣元長和，前青州驃騎府司馬、安定子臣胡世榮，太史令、盧鄉縣開國男臣趙洪慶，太史令臣胡法通，應詔左右臣張喆，員外司馬督臣曹魏祖，太史丞郭慶，太史博士臣胡仲和等，或器標民譽，或術兼世業，並能顯微闡幽，表同錄異，詳考古今，共成此曆。

translations.literal: The Left Household Gentleman of the Luminous Hall Lu Daoyue, the Minister of Grand Agriculture and Marquis of Pengcheng Li Xie, the Left Household Gentleman of the Luminous Hall and Chief Rectifier of Eastern Yong Province Pei Xianbo, the Attendant-in-Ordinary and Chief Rectifier of Western Yan Province Wen Zisheng, the Chief Clerk of the Grand Marshal's Office Lu Cao, the Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and Baron of Chengyang Lu Yuanming, the Secretariat Gentleman Li Tonggui, the former Secretariat Gentleman Xing Ziming, the Secretariat Gentleman Yuwen Zhongzhi, the former Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works and Baron of Jiankang Yuan Zhongjun, the Grand Chancellor's Legal Section Staff Member Du Bi, the Left Central Military Section Director of the Masters of Writing and Baron of Dingyang Li Puji, the Initiation Section Director of the Masters of Writing Xin Shu, the Sacrificial Section Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Changhe, the former Agile Cavalry General's Staff Major of Qing Province and Viscount of Anding Hu Shirong, the Director of Astronomy and Baron of Luxiang Zhao Hongqing, the Director of Astronomy Hu Fatong, the Imperial Rescript Attendant Zhang Zhe, the Supernumerary Staff Major Cao Weizu, the Assistant Director of Astronomy Guo Qing, the Erudite of Astronomy Hu Zhonghe, and others—some marked by reputation among the people, some combining arts with hereditary profession—all able to display the subtle and clarify the obscure, set forth sameness and record difference, examine antiquity and the present in detail, and together complete this calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Daoyue, Left Household Gentleman of the Luminous Hall; Li Xie, Minister of Grand Agriculture and Marquis of Pengcheng; Pei Xianbo, Left Household Gentleman and Chief Rectifier of Eastern Yong; Wen Zisheng, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Chief Rectifier of Western Yan; Lu Cao, Chief Clerk of the Grand Marshal's Office; Lu Yuanming, Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and Baron of Chengyang; Li Tonggui, Secretariat Gentleman; Xing Ziming, former Secretariat Gentleman; Yuwen Zhongzhi, Secretariat Gentleman; Yuan Zhongjun, former Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works and Baron of Jiankang; Du Bi, Legal Section staff member to the Grand Chancellor; Li Puji, Left Central Military Section Director and Baron of Dingyang; Xin Shu, Initiation Section Director; Yuan Changhe, Sacrificial Section Director; Hu Shirong, former Staff Major of the Qingzhou Agile Cavalry command and Viscount of Anding; Zhao Hongqing, Director of Astronomy and Baron of Luxiang; Hu Fatong, Director of Astronomy; Zhang Zhe, Imperial Rescript Attendant; Cao Weizu, Supernumerary Staff Major; Guo Qing, Assistant Director of Astronomy; Hu Zhonghe, Erudite of Astronomy—and others, some renowned for talent, others inheriting calendrical arts from their families—all joined to elucidate the obscure, reconcile divergent views, and examine past and present records, together completing this calendar.

sentences.zh: 甲為日始，子實天正，命曆置元，宜從此起。

translations.literal: Jia is the beginning of days, zi is truly the celestial standard; ordering the calendar and setting the origin should begin from here.
translations.idiomatic: Jia marks the start of the day-cycle, and zi is the true celestial commencement; in establishing a calendar and fixing its epoch, one should begin from these.

sentences.zh: 運屬興和，以年號為目，豈獨太初表於漢代，景初冠於魏曆而已。

translations.literal: Fortune belongs to Xinghe; taking the era name as its heading—is it only the Taichu that marked the Han, or the Jingchu that crowned the Wei calendar.
translations.idiomatic: As fortune now belongs to the Xinghe era, the calendar should take that reign title as its designation—just as the Taichu era name distinguished the Han calendar, and the Jingchu crowned that of Wei.

sentences.zh: 謹以封呈，乞付有司，依術施用。

translations.literal: We respectfully present this sealed, begging that it be handed to the appropriate offices to apply according to the method.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully submit this in sealed form, requesting that the appropriate offices receive it and put its methods into practice.

sentences.zh: 詔以新曆示齊獻武王田曹參軍信都芳，芳關通曆術，駁業興曰：「今年十二月二十日，新曆歲星在營室十三度，[2]順，疾；

translations.literal: An edict showed the new calendar to Xin Du Fang, Field Section staff member to the Qi Prince Xianwu; Fang, versed in calendrical arts, refuted Li Yexing, saying: "On the twentieth day of the twelfth month this year, the new calendar places the Year Star in Encampment at thirteen degrees, [2] direct, swift;
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed that the new calendar be shown to Xin Du Fang, staff member of the Field Section under the Qi Prince Xianwu. Fang, well versed in calendrical computation, challenged Li Yexing: "On the twentieth day of the twelfth month this year, the new calendar places Jupiter in Encampment at thirteen degrees, [2] in direct motion, swift;

sentences.zh: 天上歲星在營室十一度。

translations.literal: the Year Star in the sky is in Encampment at eleven degrees.
translations.idiomatic: yet Jupiter in the sky is in Encampment at eleven degrees.

sentences.zh: 今月二十日，新曆鎮星在角十一度，留；

translations.literal: On the twentieth of this month, the new calendar places the Quelling Star in Horn at eleven degrees, stationary;
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth of this month, the new calendar places Saturn in Horn at eleven degrees, stationary;

sentences.zh: 天上鎮星在亢四度，留。

translations.literal: the Quelling Star in the sky is in Neck at four degrees, stationary.
translations.idiomatic: yet Saturn in the sky is in Neck at four degrees, stationary.

sentences.zh: 今月二十日，新曆太白在斗二十五度，晨見，逆行；

translations.literal: On the twentieth of this month, the new calendar places Great White in Dipper at twenty-five degrees, morning appearance, retrograde;
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth of this month, the new calendar places Venus in Dipper at twenty-five degrees, visible in the morning, in retrograde;

sentences.zh: 天上太白在斗二十一度，逆行。

translations.literal: Great White in the sky is in Dipper at twenty-one degrees, retrograde.
translations.idiomatic: yet Venus in the sky is in Dipper at twenty-one degrees, in retrograde.

sentences.zh: 便為差殊。」

translations.literal: Thus there is discrepancy."
translations.idiomatic: These are clear discrepancies."

sentences.zh: 業興對曰：

translations.literal: Li Yexing replied:
translations.idiomatic: Li Yexing replied:

sentences.zh: 歲星行天，伺候以來八九餘年，恒不及二度。

translations.literal: The Year Star traversing Heaven, since observation began eight or nine years and more, has constantly fallen short by two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter's course through the heavens, as observed over the past eight or nine years, has consistently lagged by about two degrees.

sentences.zh: 今新曆加二度。

translations.literal: Now the new calendar adds two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar therefore adds two degrees.

sentences.zh: 至於夕伏晨見，纖毫無爽。

translations.literal: As for evening hiding and morning appearance, not a hair's breadth of error.
translations.idiomatic: As for its evening setting and morning rising, there is not the slightest discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 今日仰看，如覺二度，及其出沒，還應如術。

translations.literal: Looking up today, it seems like two degrees, but when it sets and rises, it still accords with the method.
translations.idiomatic: Observed today, it may seem off by two degrees, yet when it sets and rises, it will still conform to the computational method.

sentences.zh: 鎮星，自造壬子元以來，歲常不及，故加壬子七度，亦知猶不及五度，適欲并加，恐出沒頓校十度、十日，將來永用，不合處多。

translations.literal: The Quelling Star, since the creation of the renzi origin, year by year has constantly fallen short; therefore seven degrees were added to the renzi calendar, yet it is also known still to fall short by five degrees; just when one wishes to add them all, one fears that at setting and rising there would suddenly be a correction of ten degrees and ten days; for perpetual future use, there would be many places of non-conformity.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn, since the renzi epoch was established, has year after year lagged behind observation; seven degrees were therefore added to the renzi calendar, yet it still falls short by about five degrees. To add the full amount at once would risk sudden corrections of ten degrees and ten days at rising and setting—creating many discrepancies if the calendar were used indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 太白之行，頓疾頓遲，取其會歸而已。

translations.literal: Great White's motion, now swift now slow, takes only its conjunction-return.
translations.idiomatic: Venus moves now swiftly, now slowly; the calendar need only capture its points of conjunction.

sentences.zh: 近十二月二十日，晨見東方，新舊二曆推之，分寸不異。

translations.literal: Recently on the twentieth of the twelfth month, morning appearance in the east—the old and new calendars push it, not a fen or cun different.
translations.idiomatic: On the recent twentieth of the twelfth month, when it appeared in the morning in the east, the old and new calendars agreed to the minutest fraction.

sentences.zh: 行星三日，頓校四度。

translations.literal: The moving star in three days suddenly corrects four degrees.
translations.idiomatic: A planet may shift four degrees in the space of three days.

sentences.zh: 如此之事，無年不有，至其伏見，還依術法。

translations.literal: Matters like this occur every year without fail; when it comes to hiding and appearance, it still follows the computational method.
translations.idiomatic: Such variations occur every year; yet when planets set and rise, they still conform to the computational rules.

sentences.zh: 又芳唯嫌十二月二十日星有前却。

translations.literal: Moreover Fang only objects that on the twentieth of the twelfth month the stars have advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Fang's sole objection concerns the forward and backward discrepancies of the stars on the twentieth of the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 業興推步已來，三十餘載，上算千載之日月星辰有見經史者，與涼州趙𢾺、劉義隆廷尉卿何承天、劉駿南徐州從事史祖沖之參校，業興甲子元曆長於三曆一倍。

translations.literal: Since Li Yexing's pushing steps, more than thirty years, calculating upward a thousand years of sun, moon, stars, and planets recorded in the classics and histories, he cross-checked with Liangzhou's Zhao Fei, Liu Yilong's Minister of Justice He Chengtian, and Liu Jun's Southern Xuzhou Attendant Clerk Zu Chongzhi; Li Yexing's jiazi-origin calendar excels the three calendars by a factor of two.
translations.idiomatic: For more than thirty years since he began his computations, Li Yexing has calculated backward through a millennium of solar, lunar, and planetary positions recorded in the classics and histories, comparing his results with the work of Zhao Fei of Liangzhou, He Chengtian, Minister of Justice under Liu Yilong, and Zu Chongzhi, Attendant Clerk of Southern Xuzhou under Liu Jun. His jiazi-epoch calendar proves twice as accurate as all three of theirs.

sentences.zh: 考洛京已來四十餘歲，五星出沒，歲星、鎮星、太白，業興曆首尾恒中，及有差處，不過一日二日、一度兩度；

translations.literal: Examining from Luoyang to the present more than forty years, the five stars' hiding and appearance—Year Star, Quelling Star, Great White—Li Yexing's calendar from beginning to end is constantly centered; where there is discrepancy, it does not exceed one or two days, one or two degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Examining the past forty-odd years since Luoyang was the capital, the risings and settings of the five planets—Jupiter, Saturn, and Venus—Li Yexing's calendar has consistently matched at both beginning and end; where discrepancies occur, they amount to no more than a day or two, a degree or two;

sentences.zh: 三曆之失，動校十日十度。

translations.literal: the three calendars' errors, in motion correct ten days and ten degrees.
translations.idiomatic: whereas the three rival calendars err by as much as ten days and ten degrees.

sentences.zh: 熒惑一星，伏見體自無常，或不應度。

translations.literal: The Sparkling Deluder star alone, in hiding and appearance its form is naturally inconstant, sometimes not matching the degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Mars alone is inherently irregular in its appearances and disappearances, sometimes failing to match the predicted degrees.

sentences.zh: 祖沖之曆多甲子曆十日六度，何承天曆不及三十日二十九度；

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi's calendar exceeds the jiazi calendar by ten days and six degrees; He Chengtian's calendar falls short by thirty days and twenty-nine degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi's calendar runs ten days and six degrees ahead of the jiazi calendar; He Chengtian's falls short by thirty days and twenty-nine degrees;

sentences.zh: 今曆還與壬子同，不有加增。

translations.literal: the present calendar still agrees with renzi, without addition or increase.
translations.idiomatic: the present calendar still agrees with the renzi system, without further adjustment.

sentences.zh: 辰星一星，沒多見少，及其見時，與曆無舛，今此亦依壬子元不改。

translations.literal: The Chronogram Star alone hides much and appears little; when it appears, it has no conflict with the calendar; the present calendar also follows the renzi origin without change.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury hides often and appears rarely; when it does appear, it matches the calendar without error. The present calendar likewise follows the renzi epoch unchanged.

sentences.zh: 太白、辰星，唯起夕合為異。

translations.literal: Great White and the Chronogram Star differ only in evening rising and conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Venus and Mercury differ only in their evening risings and conjunctions.

sentences.zh: 業興以天道高遠，測步難精，五行伏留，推考不易，人目仰窺，未能盡密，但取其見伏大歸，略其中間小謬，如此曆便可行。

translations.literal: Li Yexing considers that the Heavenly Way is lofty and far; measurement and steps are hard to refine; the five phases' hiding and lingering, pushing and examining are not easy; the human eye looking up cannot be fully precise; one need only take their great return of appearance and hiding, omitting small errors in the middle—such a calendar can then be used.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yexing holds that the Heavenly Way is vast and remote, precise measurement difficult, and the hiding and lingering of the five planets hard to compute fully; the naked eye cannot achieve perfect accuracy. One need only capture the broad pattern of their appearances and disappearances, allowing for minor intermediate errors—such a calendar can serve well enough.

sentences.zh: 若專據所見之驗，不取出沒之效，則曆數之道其幾廢矣。

translations.literal: If one relies solely on what is seen as verification, not taking the effect of hiding and appearance, then the way of calendrical numbers would nearly be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: If one relied solely on momentary observations without considering risings and settings, the art of calendrical computation would be all but abandoned.

sentences.zh: 夫造曆者，節之與朔貫穿於千年之間，閏餘斗分推之於毫釐之內。

translations.literal: Those who make calendars: the nodes and new moons penetrate through a thousand years; intercalary surplus and dipper parts are pushed within a hair's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar-makers must thread solar terms and new moons through a thousand years, and push intercalary remainders and fractional parts to the finest precision.

sentences.zh: 必使盈縮得衷，間限數合，周日小分不殊錙銖，陽曆陰曆纖芥無爽，損益之數驗之交會，日所居度考之月蝕，上推下減，先定眾條，然後曆元可求，猶甲子難值。

translations.literal: One must make fullness and contraction obtain the mean, interval limits and numbers agree, circuit-day small parts not differing by a zhu or li, solar and lunar calendars not off by a mustard seed, the numbers of decrease and increase verified at conjunction, the degrees the sun occupies examined at lunar eclipse, pushing up and reducing down, first fixing the many rules—then the calendar origin can be sought, yet as hard to hit as a jiazi year.
translations.idiomatic: Fullness and contraction must strike the true mean; interval limits and numerical relations must align; fractional parts of the circuit-day must agree to the smallest unit; solar and lunar reckonings must be exact; adjustment figures must be verified at conjunctions; the sun's position must be tested against lunar eclipses. By extrapolating upward and reducing downward, fixing all rules first, the calendar epoch may then be determined—yet as elusive as a perfect jiazi alignment.

sentences.zh: 又雖值甲子，復有差分，如此踳駁，參錯不等。

translations.literal: Moreover even when one hits jiazi, there are again fractional discrepancies; thus contradictory, interwoven unequally.
translations.idiomatic: Even when a jiazi alignment is achieved, fractional discrepancies remain; systems contradict and overlap without ever fully agreeing.

sentences.zh: 今曆發元甲子，七率同遵，合璧連珠，其言不失。

translations.literal: The present calendar sets its origin in jiazi; the seven rates all follow together; joined jades and strung pearls—its statements do not miss.
translations.idiomatic: The present calendar takes its origin in a jiazi year; the seven computational rates all conform together, like jades joined and pearls strung—its principles hold true.

sentences.zh: 法理分明，情謂為可。

translations.literal: The principles and methods are clear; in feeling we say it is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Its principles and methods are clear; we believe it should be adopted.

sentences.zh: 如芳所言，信亦不謬。

translations.literal: As Fang says, truly it is not erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's observations are indeed not without merit.

sentences.zh: 但一合之裏星度不驗者，至若合終必還。

translations.literal: But within one conjunction where star-degrees are not verified, when the conjunction ends they must return.
translations.idiomatic: Yet where planetary degrees fail to match within a single conjunction, they will invariably realign by the conjunction's end.

sentences.zh: 依術，鎮星前年十二月二十日見差五度，今日差三度；

translations.literal: According to the method, the Quelling Star on the twentieth of the twelfth month two years ago showed discrepancy of five degrees; today the discrepancy is three degrees;
translations.idiomatic: By the computational method, Saturn on the twentieth of the twelfth month two years ago showed a five-degree discrepancy; today the discrepancy is three degrees;

sentences.zh: 太白前差四度，今全無差。

translations.literal: Great White previously differed by four degrees; now there is no discrepancy at all.
translations.idiomatic: Venus previously differed by four degrees; now there is no discrepancy at all.

sentences.zh: 以此準之，見伏之驗，尋效可知，將來永用，大體無失。

translations.literal: Using this as standard, the verification of appearance and hiding, seeking the effect one can know; for perpetual future use, in the great pattern there is no loss.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by this standard, the verification of risings and settings will soon become clear; for long-term use, the calendar will hold firm in its essentials.

sentences.zh: 芳又云，以去年十二月中算新曆，其鎮星以十二月二十日在角十一度留，天上在亢四度留，是新曆差天五度；

translations.literal: Fang also said, calculating the new calendar from last year's twelfth month, its Quelling Star on the twentieth of the twelfth month is stationary in Horn at eleven degrees, while in the sky it is stationary in Neck at four degrees—thus the new calendar differs from Heaven by five degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Fang also argued that, calculating from last year's twelfth month, the new calendar places Saturn stationary in Horn at eleven degrees on the twentieth, while in the sky it is stationary in Neck at four degrees—the new calendar thus differing from the heavens by five degrees;

sentences.zh: 太白、歲星並各有差。

translations.literal: Great White and the Year Star each also have discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Venus and Jupiter each show discrepancies as well.

sentences.zh: 校於壬子舊曆，鎮星差天五度，太白歲星亦各有差，是舊曆差天為多，新曆差天為少。

translations.literal: Compared with the old renzi calendar, the Quelling Star differs from Heaven by five degrees, Great White and Year Star also each have discrepancy—the old calendar's difference from Heaven is greater, the new calendar's difference from Heaven is less.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the old renzi calendar, which also places Saturn five degrees off, along with discrepancies for Venus and Jupiter, the old calendar deviates more from the heavens, the new calendar less.

sentences.zh: 凡造曆者，皆須積年累日，依法候天，知其疏密，然後審其近者，用作曆術。

translations.literal: All who make calendars must accumulate years and pile up days, observing Heaven according to method, knowing its sparse and dense, then examine which is nearer and use it as calendrical method.
translations.idiomatic: All calendar-makers must accumulate observations over many years, watching the heavens by established methods to learn where computations are loose or tight, then adopt whichever approach proves closest.

sentences.zh: 不可一月兩月之間，能正是非。

translations.literal: One cannot in the space of one or two months determine right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: One cannot settle such questions in the space of a month or two.

sentences.zh: 若如熒惑行天七百七十九日，一遲、一疾、一留、一逆、一順、一伏、一見之法，七頭一終；

translations.literal: If like the Sparkling Deluder traversing Heaven in seven hundred seventy-nine days—one slow, one swift, one stationary, one retrograde, one direct, one hidden, one appearance—the method of seven heads completing one cycle;
translations.idiomatic: Consider Mars, which traverses the heavens in seven hundred seventy-nine days through one phase each of slowness, swiftness, station, retrogradation, direct motion, hiding, and appearance—seven phases completing one cycle;

sentences.zh: 太白行天五百八十三日，晨夕之法，七頭一終；

translations.literal: Great White traversing Heaven in five hundred eighty-three days, the method of morning and evening, seven heads completing one cycle;
translations.idiomatic: Venus, traversing the heavens in five hundred eighty-three days through its morning and evening appearances, seven phases completing one cycle;

sentences.zh: 歲星行天三百九十八日，七頭一終；

translations.literal: the Year Star traversing Heaven in three hundred ninety-eight days, seven heads completing one cycle;
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter traverses the heavens in three hundred ninety-eight days, seven phases completing one cycle;

sentences.zh: 鎮星行天三百七十八日，七頭一終；

translations.literal: the Quelling Star traversing Heaven in three hundred seventy-eight days, seven heads completing one cycle;
translations.idiomatic: Saturn traverses the heavens in three hundred seventy-eight days, seven phases completing one cycle;

sentences.zh: 辰星行天一百一十五日，晨夕之法，七頭一終。

translations.literal: the Chronogram Star traversing Heaven in one hundred fifteen days, the method of morning and evening, seven heads completing one cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury traverses the heavens in one hundred fifteen days through its morning and evening appearances, seven phases completing one cycle.

sentences.zh: 造曆者必須測知七頭，然後作術。

translations.literal: Calendar-makers must measure and know the seven heads, then compose the method.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar-makers must observe and master these seven phases before they can construct their methods.

sentences.zh: 得七頭者造曆為近，不得頭者其曆甚疏，皆非一二日能知是非。

translations.literal: Those who obtain the seven heads make calendars that are near; those who do not obtain the heads—their calendars are very sparse; none can know right and wrong in a day or two.
translations.idiomatic: Those who master the seven phases produce calendars that closely match the heavens; those who do not produce very loose ones. In neither case can right and wrong be determined in a day or two.

sentences.zh: 自五帝三代以來及秦、漢、魏、晉，造曆者皆積年久測，術乃可觀。

translations.literal: From the Five Emperors and Three Dynasties onward through Qin, Han, Wei, and Jin, calendar-makers all accumulated years of long observation; only then were their methods worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: From the Five Emperors and Three Dynasties through Qin, Han, Wei, and Jin, every successful calendar-maker accumulated years of observation before his methods proved reliable.

sentences.zh: 其倉卒造者，當時或近，不可久行。

translations.literal: Those made in haste, at the time may be near, but cannot be used for long.
translations.idiomatic: Calendars composed in haste may match the heavens briefly but cannot endure.

sentences.zh: 若三四年作者，初雖近天，多載恐失。

translations.literal: If made in three or four years, at first though near Heaven, over many years one fears loss.
translations.idiomatic: Even those composed over three or four years, though accurate at first, may drift over the course of many years.

sentences.zh: 今甲子新曆，業興潛構積年，雖有少差，校於壬子元曆，近天者多。

translations.literal: The present jiazi new calendar—Li Yexing secretly constructed accumulated years; though having slight discrepancy, compared with the renzi-origin calendar, it is nearer Heaven in more respects.
translations.idiomatic: The present jiazi calendar, which Li Yexing built upon years of accumulated computation, shows only minor discrepancies; compared with the renzi calendar, it accords more closely with the heavens.

sentences.zh: 若久而驗天，十年二十年間，比壬子元曆，三星行天，其差為密。

translations.literal: If over time one verifies Heaven, within ten or twenty years, compared with the renzi-origin calendar, the three stars traversing Heaven—their discrepancy will be dense, i.e., small.
translations.idiomatic: If verified over ten or twenty years, the three planets' courses will prove far closer to the heavens than under the renzi calendar.

translations.literal: The Prince Xianwu reported this upward; an edict handed it to the outer offices for implementation.

sentences.zh: 推月朔弦望術第一

translations.literal: Method One for computing new moon, first quarter, full moon, and last quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure I: Computing New Moon, First Quarter, Full Moon, and Last Quarter.

sentences.zh: 推積月術曰：置入紀以來盡所求年，減一，以章月乘之，章歲如一，所得為積月，不盡為閏餘。

translations.literal: The method for computing accumulated months says: set in from the era beginning through the year sought, subtract one, multiply by rule-months, as rule-years yields one—the result is accumulated months; what is not exhausted is the intercalary remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To compute accumulated months: from the era's opening through the year sought, subtract one, multiply by the rule-months, divide by the rule-years; the quotient is accumulated months and the remainder is the intercalary surplus.

sentences.zh: 閏餘三百五十五以上，其年有閏。

translations.literal: If the intercalary remainder is 355 or above, that year has an intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: When the intercalary remainder reaches 355 or more, the year receives an intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 餘五百一十五以上，進退在天正十一月前後，以冬至定之。

translations.literal: If the remainder is 515 or above, advance or retreat before or after the celestial first month's eleventh month; fix it by the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: When the remainder is 515 or higher, adjust placement around the eleventh month of the celestial year, using the winter solstice as the criterion.

sentences.zh: 推積日術曰：以通數乘積月，為朔積分，日法如一，為積日，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: The method for computing accumulated days says: multiply accumulated months by the communication number to obtain new-moon accumulated parts; as the day factor yields one, this gives accumulated days; what is not exhausted is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To compute accumulated days: multiply accumulated months by the communication number for the new-moon accumulated fraction; divide by the day factor for accumulated days, with the remainder as the small remainder.

sentences.zh: 以六旬去積日，不盡為大餘。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated days; what is not exhausted is the large remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Cast out full sexagenary cycles from the accumulated days; what remains is the large remainder.

sentences.zh: 命大餘以紀，

translations.literal: Assign the large remainder by era,
translations.idiomatic: Count the large remainder from the era marker,

sentences.zh: 〈今命以甲戌紀。〉

translations.literal: 〈Now assign it using the jiaxu era.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The count is currently taken from the jiaxu era.〉

sentences.zh: 算外，即所求年天正十一月朔日。

translations.literal: Beyond the tally—and that is the new-moon day of the celestial first month's eleventh month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: One day beyond the count gives the new moon of the eleventh month (celestial first month) in the year sought.

sentences.zh: 求次月朔術曰：加大餘二十九、小餘十一萬六百四十七，滿除如上，命以紀，算外，即次月朔日。

translations.literal: The method for finding the next month's new moon says: add to the large remainder twenty-nine and to the small remainder 110,647; when full, remove as above; assign by era; beyond the tally—and that is the next month's new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: To find the next new moon: add 29 to the large remainder and 110,647 to the small remainder; carry overflow as before, count from the era marker, and one day beyond the tally is the next month's new moon.

sentences.zh: 其小餘滿虛分九萬七千八百八十三者，其月大；

translations.literal: If its small remainder fills the deficiency parts of 97,883, that month is long;
translations.idiomatic: If the small remainder reaches the deficiency-part constant of 97,883, the month is long;

sentences.zh: 減者，其月小。

translations.literal: If reduced, that month is short.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise it is short.

sentences.zh: 求上下弦望術曰：加朔大餘七、小餘七萬九千七百九十四、小分一。

translations.literal: The method for finding the upper and lower quarters and full moon says: add to the new-moon large remainder seven, to the small remainder 79,794, and to the minor parts one.
translations.idiomatic: To find the first quarter, full moon, and last quarter: add 7 to the new-moon large remainder, 79,794 to the small remainder, and 1 to the minor parts.

sentences.zh: 小分滿四，從小餘；

translations.literal: When minor parts fill four, let them carry to the small remainder;
translations.idiomatic: When minor parts reach four, carry into the small remainder;

sentences.zh: 小餘滿日法，從大餘；

translations.literal: when the small remainder fills the day factor, let it carry to the large remainder;
translations.idiomatic: when the small remainder fills the day factor, carry into the large remainder;

sentences.zh: 大餘滿六十，去之，命以紀，算外，[14]即上弦日。

translations.literal: when the large remainder fills sixty, remove it; assign by era; beyond the tally,[14] and that is the first-quarter day.
translations.idiomatic: when the large remainder reaches sixty, cast it out, count from the era marker, and one day beyond the tally[14] is the first-quarter day.

sentences.zh: 又加，得望、下弦、後月朔。

translations.literal: Add again to obtain full moon, last quarter, and the next month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the addition to get the full moon, last quarter, and the following new moon.

sentences.zh: 推二十四氣閏術第二

translations.literal: Method Two for computing the twenty-four qi and intercalation.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure II: The Twenty-Four Solar Terms and Intercalation.

sentences.zh: 推二十四氣術曰：置入紀以來盡所求年，減一，以餘數乘之，蔀法如一，為積沒，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: The method for computing the twenty-four qi says: set in from the era beginning through the year sought, subtract one, multiply by the remainder number, as the obscuration factor yields one—this gives accumulated submergence; what is not exhausted is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To compute the twenty-four qi: from the era's opening through the year sought, subtract one, multiply by the remainder number, and divide by the obscuration factor; the quotient is accumulated submergence and the remainder is the small remainder.

sentences.zh: 以六旬去積沒，不盡為大餘，命以紀，算外，即所求年天正十一月冬至日。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated submergence; what is not exhausted is the large remainder; assign by era; beyond the tally—and that is the winter-solstice day of the celestial first month's eleventh month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Cast out sexagenary cycles from the accumulated submergence; the remainder is the large remainder; count from the era marker, and one day beyond the tally is the winter solstice of the eleventh month (celestial first month) in the year sought.

sentences.zh: 求次氣術術曰：加大餘十五、小餘三千六百八十四、小分一，小分滿小分法二十四，從小餘；

translations.literal: The method for finding the next qi says: add to the large remainder fifteen, to the small remainder 3,684, and to the minor parts one; when minor parts fill the minor-parts divisor of twenty-four, let them carry to the small remainder;
translations.idiomatic: To find the next solar term: add 15 to the large remainder, 3,684 to the small remainder, and 1 to the minor parts; when minor parts reach the minor-parts divisor of 24, carry into the small remainder;

sentences.zh: 小餘滿蔀法，從大餘一，命如上，[15]算外，即次氣日。

translations.literal: when the small remainder fills the obscuration factor, let one carry to the large remainder; assign as above; beyond the tally,[15] and that is the next qi day.
translations.idiomatic: when the small remainder fills the obscuration factor, carry 1 into the large remainder; count as before, and one day beyond the tally[15] is the next solar-term day.

sentences.zh: 推閏術曰：以閏餘減章歲，餘以歲中十二乘之，滿章閏二百七得一，月餘半法以上亦得一月，數起天正十一月，算外，即閏月。

translations.literal: The method for computing intercalation says: subtract rule-years from the intercalary remainder; multiply the remainder by mid-year twelve; when full, as rule-intercalations two hundred seven yields one; if the month-remainder is half the divisor or above, also obtain one month; count from the celestial first month's eleventh month; beyond the tally—and that is the intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: To determine intercalation: subtract the rule-years from the intercalary remainder, multiply by twelve (mid-year qi), divide by the rule-intercalations of 207; if the month-remainder is at least half the divisor, count another month; start from the eleventh month (celestial first month), and one beyond the tally marks the intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 閏月有進退，[16]以無中氣定之。

translations.literal: The intercalary month may advance or retreat;[16] fix it by the absence of a mid-term qi.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary months may be placed forward or back;[16] placement is fixed where no mid-term qi falls.

sentences.zh: 推閏又法術曰：以歲中乘閏餘，如章閏得一，[17]盈章中六千七百四十四，數起冬至，算外，中氣終閏月也。

translations.literal: Another method for computing intercalation says: multiply the intercalary remainder by mid-year; as rule-intercalations yields one;[17] when full, rule-center six thousand seven hundred forty-four; count from the winter solstice; beyond the tally—the mid-term qi ends and the intercalary month begins.
translations.idiomatic: Alternate intercalation method: multiply the intercalary remainder by twelve and divide by the rule-intercalations of 207;[17] when the product exceeds the rule-center of 6,744, count from the winter solstice—one beyond the tally marks where the mid-term qi ends and the intercalary month begins.

sentences.zh: 盈中氣在朔若二日，即前月閏。

translations.literal: If the surplus mid-term qi falls on the new moon or within two days, then the prior month is intercalary.
translations.idiomatic: When the excess mid-term qi coincides with the new moon or within two days of it, the intercalary month is placed in the preceding month.

sentences.zh: 冬至十一月中 小寒十二月節 大寒十二月中 立春正月節

translations.literal: Winter Solstice—mid-eleventh month; Lesser Cold—twelfth-month node; Greater Cold—mid-twelfth month; Start of Spring—first-month node.
translations.idiomatic: Winter Solstice: mid-11th month. Lesser Cold: 12th-month solar node. Greater Cold: mid-12th month. Start of Spring: 1st-month solar node.

sentences.zh: 雨水正月中 驁蟄二月節 春分二月中 清明三月節

translations.literal: Rain Water—mid-first month; Awakening of Insects—second-month node; Spring Equinox—mid-second month; Clear and Bright—third-month node.
translations.idiomatic: Rain Water: mid-1st month. Awakening of Insects: 2nd-month solar node. Spring Equinox: mid-2nd month. Clear and Bright: 3rd-month solar node.

translations.idiomatic: Grain Rain: mid-3rd month. Start of Summer: 4th-month solar node. Lesser Fullness: mid-4th month. Grain in Ear: 5th-month solar node.

translations.idiomatic: Summer Solstice: mid-5th month. Lesser Heat: 6th-month solar node. Greater Heat: mid-6th month. Start of Autumn: 7th-month solar node.

translations.idiomatic: End of Heat: mid-7th month. White Dew: 8th-month solar node. Autumn Equinox: mid-8th month. Cold Dew: 9th-month solar node.

sentences.zh: 霜降九月中 立冬十月節 小雪十月中 大雪十一月節

translations.literal: Frost Descent—mid-ninth month; Start of Winter—tenth-month node; Lesser Snow—mid-tenth month; Greater Snow—eleventh-month node.
translations.idiomatic: Frost Descent: mid-9th month. Start of Winter: 10th-month solar node. Lesser Snow: mid-10th month. Greater Snow: 11th-month solar node.

sentences.zh: 推合朔却去度表裏術第三

translations.literal: Method Three for computing syzygy, retreat from the crossing, and degrees on the outer and inner sides.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure III: Syzygy, Crossing Distance, and Inner/Outer Ecliptic Position.

sentences.zh: 推合朔却去交度術曰：置入紀以來朔積分，又以所入紀交會差分并之，

translations.literal: The method for computing syzygy and retreat from the crossing degree says: set in the new-moon accumulated parts from the era beginning, and also combine with the conjunction-difference parts of the era entered,
translations.idiomatic: To compute syzygy and distance from the lunar node: take the new-moon accumulated fraction from the era's opening and add the conjunction-difference fraction for the era entered,

sentences.zh: 〈甲戌紀交會差分二千六百五十二萬二千六百四十九。〉

translations.literal: 〈For the jiaxu era, the conjunction-difference parts are 26,522,649.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Jiaxu-era conjunction-difference fraction: 26,522,649.〉

sentences.zh: 以會通去之，所得為積交；

translations.literal: Remove the conjunction communication from it; what is obtained is accumulated crossing;
translations.idiomatic: subtract the conjunction-communication constant; the quotient is the accumulated crossings;

sentences.zh: 不盡者，以日法約之，為度，不盡者為度餘，即所求年天正十一月朔却去交度及度餘。

translations.literal: what is not exhausted, reduce it by the day factor to obtain degrees; what is not exhausted is the degree remainder—and that is the syzygy's retreat from the crossing degree and degree remainder on the new-moon day of the celestial first month's eleventh month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: the remainder, divided by the day factor, gives degrees with a degree remainder—this is the crossing distance at the new moon of the eleventh month (celestial first month) in the year sought.

translations.literal: Conjunction difference: 115 degrees; degree remainder 203,874.
translations.idiomatic: Conjunction-difference: 115°; degree remainder 203,874.

sentences.zh: 求次月却去交度術曰：加度二十九、度餘十一萬六百四十七，度餘滿日法從度，度滿會數去之，亦除其會餘，即次月朔却去交度及度餘。

translations.literal: The method for finding the next month's retreat from the crossing degree says: add to degrees twenty-nine and to degree remainder 110,647; when the degree remainder fills the day factor, let it carry to degrees; when degrees fill the conjunction number, remove it, and also remove its conjunction remainder—and that is the next month's new-moon retreat from the crossing degree and degree remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To find the next month's node distance: add 29 degrees and 110,647 to the degree remainder; carry overflow from the degree remainder through the day factor into degrees; when degrees reach the conjunction number, subtract it and the conjunction remainder—the result is the next new moon's crossing distance and degree remainder.

sentences.zh: 求望却去交度術曰：加度十四、度餘十五萬九千五百八十八半，滿除如上，即望却去交度及度餘。

translations.literal: The method for finding the full moon's retreat from the crossing degree says: add to degrees fourteen and to degree remainder 159,588 and a half; when full, remove as above—and that is the full moon's retreat from the crossing degree and degree remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To find the full moon's node distance: add 14 degrees and 159,588½ to the degree remainder; carry overflow as above—the result is the full moon's crossing distance and degree remainder.

sentences.zh: 推月在日道表裏術曰：置入紀以來朔積分，又以紀交會差分并之，倍會通去之，餘以會通減之，得一減者，為月在日道裏；

translations.literal: The method for computing whether the moon is on the outer or inner side of the sun's path says: set in the new-moon accumulated parts from the era beginning, and also combine with the era's conjunction-difference parts; remove double the conjunction communication; subtract the remainder by the conjunction communication; when one subtraction is obtained, the moon is on the inner side of the sun's path;
translations.idiomatic: To determine whether the moon lies north or south of the ecliptic: take the new-moon accumulated fraction from the era's opening and add the era's conjunction-difference fraction; cast out double the conjunction-communication constant; subtract the conjunction communication from the remainder; if one subtraction succeeds, the moon is south of the ecliptic;

sentences.zh: 無所得者，為月在日道表。

translations.literal: When nothing is obtained, the moon is on the outer side of the sun's path.
translations.idiomatic: If no subtraction succeeds, the moon is north of the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 求次月表裏術曰：加次月度及度餘，加表滿會數及會數餘，則在裏；

translations.literal: The method for finding the next month's outer or inner side says: add the next month's degrees and degree remainder; when adding from the outer side fills the conjunction number and conjunction-number remainder, then it is on the inner side;
translations.idiomatic: To find the next month's position: add the next month's degrees and degree remainder; if starting from the outer side the conjunction number and its remainder are filled, the moon is on the inner side;

sentences.zh: 加裏滿會數及會餘，則在表。

translations.literal: When adding from the inner side fills the conjunction number and conjunction remainder, then it is on the outer side.
translations.idiomatic: If starting from the inner side the conjunction number and remainder are filled, the moon is on the outer side.

sentences.zh: 推交道所在日術曰：以十一月朔却去交度及餘減會數及會餘，會餘若不足減者，減一度，加日法乃減之；

translations.literal: The method for computing the day on which the crossing path lies says: subtract the conjunction number and conjunction remainder by the eleventh-month new moon's retreat from the crossing degree and remainder; if the conjunction remainder is insufficient to subtract, subtract one degree and add the day factor, then subtract;
translations.idiomatic: To find the day of nodal crossing: subtract the eleventh-month new moon's crossing distance and remainder from the conjunction number and conjunction remainder; if the conjunction remainder is too small, borrow one degree and add the day factor before subtracting;

sentences.zh: 又以十一月朔小餘加之，滿日法從度，餘為度餘，即是天正十一月朔前去交度及餘。

translations.literal: Also add the eleventh-month new moon's small remainder; when full, let it carry to degrees; the remainder is the degree remainder—and this is the retreat from the crossing degree and remainder before the celestial first month's eleventh-month new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Add the eleventh-month new moon's small remainder; carry overflow through the day factor into degrees, with the remainder as the degree remainder—this is the crossing distance before the new moon of the eleventh month (celestial first month).

sentences.zh: 如曆月大小除之，起天正月十一月，不滿月者為入月，算外，交道所在日。

translations.literal: Remove by long and short months of the calendar, starting from the celestial first month's eleventh month; what does not fill a month is the entered month; beyond the tally—and that is the day on which the crossing path lies.
translations.idiomatic: Divide by the long and short months of the calendar, starting from the eleventh month (celestial first month); the partial month count is the entered month, and one day beyond the tally is the day of nodal crossing.

sentences.zh: 又以歲中乘入月小餘，日法除之，所得命以子，算外，[19]即交道所在辰。

translations.literal: Also multiply the entered month's small remainder by mid-year; divide by the day factor; assign what is obtained starting from zi; beyond the tally,[19] and that is the double-hour in which the crossing path lies.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the entered month's small remainder by mid-year (12), divide by the day factor, count from the zi hour, and one beyond the tally[19] gives the double-hour of nodal crossing.

sentences.zh: 其交在望前者，其月朔則交會，[20]望則月蝕。

translations.literal: When the crossing is before the full moon, that month's new moon then has conjunction-crossing,[20] and the full moon has a lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: When the node precedes full moon, that month brings a solar eclipse at new moon[20] and a lunar eclipse at full moon.

sentences.zh: 交在望後者，其月月蝕，後朔交會。

translations.literal: When the crossing is after the full moon, that month has a lunar eclipse, and the later new moon has conjunction-crossing.
translations.idiomatic: When the node follows full moon, the month has a lunar eclipse first and a solar eclipse at the following new moon.

sentences.zh: 交正在望者，其月月蝕既，前後朔交會。

translations.literal: When the crossing is exactly at the full moon, that month has a total lunar eclipse, and the new moons before and after have conjunction-crossing.
translations.idiomatic: When the node falls exactly at full moon, the month brings a total lunar eclipse, with solar eclipses at the adjacent new moons.

sentences.zh: 交正朔者，日蝕既，前後月望皆月蝕。

translations.literal: When the crossing is exactly at the new moon, the solar eclipse is total, and the full moons of the preceding and following months both have lunar eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: When the node falls exactly at new moon, the solar eclipse is total, and both neighboring full moons bring lunar eclipses.

sentences.zh: 求後交月及日術曰：以會數及會餘加前入月算及餘，餘滿日法從日，日如曆月大小除之，起前交月，算外，即後交月及日。

translations.literal: The method for finding the next crossing month and day says: add the conjunction number and conjunction remainder to the prior entered-month count and remainder; when the remainder fills the day factor, let it carry to days; divide days by long and short months of the calendar, starting from the prior crossing month; beyond the tally—and that is the next crossing month and day.
translations.idiomatic: To find the next crossing month and day: add the conjunction number and remainder to the prior entered-month count and remainder; carry remainder overflow through the day factor into days; divide by long and short months starting from the prior crossing month, and one beyond the tally marks the next crossing month and day.

sentences.zh: 以次放之。

translations.literal: Extend it in sequence thus.
translations.idiomatic: Continue in the same manner for successive crossings.

sentences.zh: 推交會起角術曰：其月在外道，先會後交者，虧從東南角起；

translations.literal: The method for computing the starting angle of conjunction-crossing says: when that month is on the outer path, if conjunction precedes crossing, the waning begins from the southeast corner;
translations.idiomatic: To determine the eclipse's starting corner: when the moon is on the outer path and conjunction precedes crossing, the shadow begins at the southeast limb;

sentences.zh: 先交後會者，虧從西南角起。

translations.literal: If crossing precedes conjunction, the waning begins from the southwest corner.
translations.idiomatic: If crossing precedes conjunction, the shadow begins at the southwest limb.

sentences.zh: 其月在內道，先會後交者，虧從西北角起，合交中者，蝕之既。

translations.literal: When that month is on the inner path, if conjunction precedes crossing, the waning begins from the northwest corner; when conjunction and crossing are at center, the eclipse is total.
translations.idiomatic: When the moon is on the inner path and conjunction precedes crossing, the shadow begins at the northwest limb; if conjunction and crossing coincide at center, the eclipse is total.

sentences.zh: 其月蝕在日之衝，起角亦如之。

translations.literal: When the lunar eclipse is at the sun's opposite, the starting angle is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: For lunar eclipses at opposition, the starting corner follows the same rule.

sentences.zh: 推蝕分多少術曰：其朔望去交度及度餘如入交限數一百五十八度、度餘十一萬六千五十八半以上者，以減會數及會數餘，餘為不蝕度。

translations.literal: The method for computing how much of the eclipse fraction says: if the new moon's or full moon's retreat from the crossing degree and degree remainder is like the entry-to-crossing limit number of 158 degrees and degree remainder 116,058 and a half or above, subtract the conjunction number and conjunction-number remainder—the remainder is the non-eclipse degree.
translations.idiomatic: To compute eclipse magnitude: if the new-moon or full-moon crossing distance and degree remainder reach the entry-to-crossing limit of 158° with degree remainder 116,058½ or more, subtract the conjunction number and its remainder—the remainder is the non-eclipse arc.

sentences.zh: 若朔望去交度如朔望合數十四度、度餘十五萬九千五百八十八半以下者，即是不蝕度。

translations.literal: If the new moon's or full moon's retreat from the crossing degree is like the new-moon/full-moon conjunction number of fourteen degrees and degree remainder 159,588 and a half or below, then that is the non-eclipse degree.
translations.idiomatic: If the new-moon or full-moon crossing distance is within the syzygy-conjunction number of 14° with degree remainder 159,588½ or less, that value is the non-eclipse arc.

sentences.zh: [21]皆以減十五，餘為蝕分。

translations.literal: [21]In every case subtract from fifteen; the remainder is the eclipse fraction.
translations.idiomatic: [21]Subtract each from 15; the remainder is the eclipse magnitude.

sentences.zh: [22]朔望去交度盡者，蝕之既。

translations.literal: [22]When the new moon's or full moon's retreat from the crossing degree is exhausted, the eclipse is total.
translations.idiomatic: [22]When the crossing distance at new moon or full moon reaches zero, the eclipse is total.

sentences.zh: 推合朔月蝕入遲疾曆盈縮術第四

translations.literal: Method Four for computing syzygy and lunar eclipse entry into the slow-fast sequence and excess-shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure IV: Syzygy, Lunar Eclipse, and Entry into the Slow-Fast Sequence with Excess and Shortage.

sentences.zh: 推合朔入遲疾曆術曰：置入紀以來朔積分，又以所入紀遲疾差分并之，

translations.literal: The method for computing syzygy entry into the slow-fast sequence says: set in the new-moon accumulated parts from the era beginning, and also combine with the slow-fast difference parts of the era entered,
translations.idiomatic: To compute entry into the slow-fast sequence at syzygy: take the new-moon accumulated fraction from the era's opening and add the slow-fast difference fraction for the era entered,

sentences.zh: [23]以通周去之，所得為積周；

translations.literal: [23]Remove the communication cycle from it; what is obtained is accumulated cycles;
translations.idiomatic: [23]Subtract the communication-cycle constant; the quotient is accumulated cycles;

sentences.zh: [24]不盡者，以日法約之，為日，不盡者為日餘。

translations.literal: [24]What is not exhausted, reduce it by the day factor to obtain days; what is not exhausted is the day remainder.
translations.idiomatic: [24]Divide the remainder by the day factor for days, with the leftover as the day remainder.

sentences.zh: 命日，算外，即所求年天正月十一月合朔入曆日。

translations.literal: Assign the day; beyond the tally—and that is the day of calendar entry at syzygy for the celestial first month's eleventh month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Count the day from the marker; one beyond the tally is the slow-fast sequence day for the new moon of the eleventh month (celestial first month) in the year sought.

sentences.zh: 求次月入曆日術曰：加一日、日餘二十萬三千五百四十六，日蝕滿日法從日，[25]日滿周日及周餘去之，命如上，算外，即次月入曆日。

translations.literal: The method for finding the next month's calendar-entry day says: add one day and day remainder 203,546; when the day remainder fills the day factor, let it carry to days;[25] when days fill the cycle day and cycle remainder, remove them; assign as above; beyond the tally—and that is the next month's calendar-entry day.
translations.idiomatic: To find the next month's sequence day: add 1 day and 203,546 to the day remainder; carry overflow through the day factor into days;[25] when days reach the cycle day and cycle remainder, subtract them; count as before, and one beyond the tally is the next month's sequence day.
