sentences.zh: 推合朔交會月蝕定大小餘[38]術曰：以入曆日餘乘所入曆下損益率，以小周七千五百一十三除之，所得損益盈縮積分為定積分。

translations.literal: The method for computing fixed large and small remainders for syzygy, nodal crossing, and lunar eclipse[38] says: multiply the calendar-entry day remainder by the excess-deficit rate beneath the calendar entry entered, divide by the minor circuit 7,513; what is obtained, with it increase or decrease the excess-shortage accumulated parts to make the fixed accumulated parts.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure for fixing syzygy, crossing, and eclipse remainders[38]: multiply the anomalistic day fraction by the tabulated rate below that entry, divide by the minor circuit of 7,513, and apply the result to the excess-shortage column for the corrected integral.

sentences.zh: 積分盈者，[39]以減本朔望小餘；

translations.literal: When accumulated parts are in excess,[39] subtract from the original new- or full-moon small remainder;
translations.idiomatic: If the integral is in excess,[39] subtract from the base syzygy fractional day;

sentences.zh: 縮者，加之。

translations.literal: When in shortage, add to it.
translations.idiomatic: If in shortage, add to it.

sentences.zh: 加之滿日法者，交會加時在後日；

translations.literal: If adding fills the day factor, the conjunction-crossing added hour falls on the following day;
translations.idiomatic: A carry past the day factor moves the crossing instant to the next civil day;

sentences.zh: 減之，不足減者，減一日，加日法乃減之，交會加時在前日。

translations.literal: If subtracting—when insufficient to subtract, subtract one day, add the day factor and then subtract—the conjunction-crossing added hour falls on the preceding day.
translations.idiomatic: If subtracting underflows, borrow one day, add the day factor, then subtract—the crossing instant falls on the previous day.

sentences.zh: 月蝕者，隨定大小餘[40]為定日加時。

translations.literal: For lunar eclipses, follow the fixed large and small remainders[40] as the fixed day's added hour.
translations.idiomatic: For lunar eclipses, take the clock time directly from the corrected remainder line[40].

sentences.zh: 推加時術曰：以歲中乘定小餘，日法除之，所得命以子，算外。

translations.literal: The method for computing the added hour says: multiply the fixed small remainder by mid-year, divide by the day factor; assign what is obtained starting from zi; beyond the tally.
translations.idiomatic: To name the double-hour: multiply the corrected fractional day by mid-year (12), divide by the day factor, count from the zi hour, and read one beyond the tally.

sentences.zh: 朔望加時有餘不盡者，四之，如法得一為少，二為半，三為太。

translations.literal: When new- or full-moon added hours have remainder not exhausted, quadruple it; as the divisor yields one, that is shao; two makes ban; three makes tai.
translations.idiomatic: For leftover syzygy fractions, quadruple the tail and divide by the day factor for shao, ban, or tai subdivisions.

sentences.zh: 半又有餘者，三之，如法得一為強，半法以上排成一，不滿半法棄之。

translations.literal: If ban again has remainder, triple it; as the divisor yields one, that is qiang; at half the divisor or above, advance one notch; what does not fill half the divisor, discard it.
translations.idiomatic: Triple any further tail to reach the qiang step, rounding up at half-divisor.

sentences.zh: 以強并少為少強，并半為半強，并太為太強。

translations.literal: Combine qiang with shao to make shao-qiang; combine with ban to make ban-qiang; combine with tai to make tai-qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Add qiang units to shao, ban, or tai per the classical clepsydra notation.

sentences.zh: 得二強者為少弱，以之并少為半弱，以之并半為太弱，以之并太為一辰弱。

translations.literal: Obtaining two qiang makes shao-ruo; with it combine shao to make ban-ruo; with it combine ban to make tai-ruo; with it combine tai to make one chen-ruo.
translations.idiomatic: Two qiang collapse into a weak grade, stepping through the ladder to a full weak double-hour mark.

sentences.zh: 隨所在辰而命之，即其強弱。

translations.literal: Assign by the chen where it stands—and that is its qiang or ruo.
translations.idiomatic: Read the final label against the stem hour to recover the strength grade.

sentences.zh: 日之衝為破，月常在破下蝕。

translations.literal: The sun's opposite is po; the moon, when eclipsed, is always beneath po.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's anticenter is the rupture point; the moon eclipses when it stands beneath it.

sentences.zh: 推日月合朔弦望度術第五[41] 推日度術曰：置入紀以來朔積日，以日度法一萬六千八百六十乘之，滿周天去之，餘以日度法約之為度，不盡為餘。

translations.literal: Method Five for computing the degrees of sun and moon at syzygy, first quarter, full moon, and last quarter[41] The method for computing solar degree says: set in the new-moon accumulated days from the era beginning, multiply by the day-degree factor 16,860; when full, remove the circuit of heaven; reduce the remainder by the day-degree factor to obtain degrees; what is not exhausted is the remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure V: Degrees at Syzygy, Quarters, and Full Moon[41] To compute solar longitude: multiply accumulated new-moon days by the day-degree factor of 16,860, cast out whole circuits of heaven, and divide the remainder by 16,860 for degrees and fractional parts.

sentences.zh: [42]命起牛前十二度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即所求年天正十一月朔夜半日所在度及分。

translations.literal: [42]Assign starting from twelve degrees before Ox, remove by lodge sequence; what does not fill a lodge—beyond the tally—and that is the degree and parts where the sun stands at midnight on the new moon of the celestial first month's eleventh month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: [42]Count from twelve degrees before Ox, walk through the lodges, and one beyond the tally gives the midnight solar longitude on the eleventh-month (celestial first month) new moon for the year sought.

sentences.zh: 推日度又法，術曰：置周天三百六十五度、斗分四千一百一十七，以冬至去朔日數減一，以減周天度，冬至小餘減斗分；

translations.literal: Another method for computing solar degree, the method says: set the circuit of heaven at 365 degrees and Dipper parts 4,117; subtract one from the day-count from new moon to winter solstice, and with it subtract from the circuit-of-heaven degrees; subtract the winter-solstice small remainder from the Dipper parts;
translations.idiomatic: Alternate solar-longitude method: take 365° plus 4,117 Dipper parts, subtract (days from new moon to winter solstice minus one) from the degree total and the winter-solstice fractional day from the Dipper parts;

sentences.zh: 斗分不足減者，減一度，加日度法乃減之。

translations.literal: When Dipper parts are insufficient to subtract, subtract one degree, add the day-degree factor and then subtract.
translations.idiomatic: If the Dipper parts underflow, borrow one degree and add the day-degree factor before subtracting.

sentences.zh: 命起如上，算外，即所求年天正十一月朔夜半日所在度及分。

translations.literal: Assign starting as above; beyond the tally—and that is the degree and parts where the sun stands at midnight on the new moon of the celestial first month's eleventh month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Count as above; one beyond the tally gives the midnight solar longitude on the eleventh-month new moon for the year sought.

sentences.zh: 求次月次日日所在度[43]術曰：月大者加度三十，月小者加度二十九，次日者加度一，宿次除之，逕斗除其分。

translations.literal: The method for finding the sun's degree on the next month and next day[43] says: for a long month add thirty degrees, for a short month add twenty-nine, for the next day add one degree; remove by lodge sequence; directly at Dipper remove its parts.
translations.idiomatic: To find the next month's or next day's solar longitude[43]: add 30° for a long month, 29° for a short month, or 1° for the next day; walk the lodges and subtract the Dipper-part fraction directly.

translations.literal: [Editorial note 44.]
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note 44.

sentences.zh: 推合朔日月共度術曰：以章歲五百六十二乘朔小餘，以章月六千九百五十一除之，所得為大分，不盡為小分。

translations.literal: The method for computing the shared degree of sun and moon at syzygy says: multiply the new-moon small remainder by rule-years 562; divide by rule-months 6,951; what is obtained is the large fraction; what is not exhausted is the small fraction.
translations.idiomatic: To find syzygy's shared solar-lunar longitude: multiply the new-moon fractional day by 562, divide by 6,951 for the large and small fraction parts.

sentences.zh: 以加夜半日度分，分滿日度法從度，命如上，算外，即所求年天正十一月合朔日月共度。

translations.literal: Add it to the midnight solar degree and parts; when parts fill the day-degree factor, let it carry to degrees; assign as above; beyond the tally—and that is the shared degree of sun and moon at syzygy for the celestial first month's eleventh month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Add this to the midnight solar position, carry overflow through the day-degree factor, count as above, and one beyond the tally is the shared syzygy longitude for the eleventh-month new moon.

sentences.zh: 推合朔日月共度又法，術曰：加度二十九、大分八千九百四十五、小分六千九百一十九，小分滿章月從大分；

translations.literal: Another method for computing the shared degree of sun and moon at syzygy, the method says: add twenty-nine degrees, large fraction 8,945, and small fraction 6,919; when small parts fill rule-months, let them carry to large parts;
translations.idiomatic: Alternate syzygy-longitude method: add 29°, 8,945 large parts, and 6,919 small parts, carrying small-part overflow into large parts at 6,951;

sentences.zh: 大分滿日度法從度，宿次除之，逕斗去其分，算外，即次月合朔日月共度。

translations.literal: When large parts fill the day-degree factor, let them carry to degrees; remove by lodge sequence; directly at Dipper remove its parts; beyond the tally—and that is the shared degree of sun and moon at syzygy for the next month.
translations.idiomatic: Carry large-part overflow into degrees at 16,860, walk the lodges, subtract the Dipper fraction directly, and one beyond the tally is the next month's syzygy longitude.

sentences.zh: 推月度術曰：置入紀以來朔積日，以月周二十二萬五千三百九十乘之，[45]滿周天去之。

translations.literal: The method for computing lunar degree says: set in the new-moon accumulated days from the era beginning, multiply by the lunar circuit 225,390;[45] when full, remove the circuit of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: To compute lunar longitude: multiply accumulated new-moon days by the lunar circuit of 225,390;[45] cast out whole circuits of heaven.

sentences.zh: 餘以日度法約之為度，餘為度分，命起牛前十二度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即所求年天正十一月朔夜半月所在度及分。

translations.literal: Reduce the remainder by the day-degree factor to obtain degrees; the remainder is degree-parts; assign starting from twelve degrees before Ox, remove by lodge sequence; what does not fill a lodge—beyond the tally—and that is the degree and parts where the moon stands at midnight on the new moon of the celestial first month's eleventh month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the remainder by 16,860 for degrees and parts, count from twelve degrees before Ox through the lodges, and one beyond the tally gives the midnight lunar longitude on the eleventh-month new moon.

sentences.zh: 推月度又法，術曰：以小周乘朔小餘為實，章歲乘日法為法，實如法得一為度；

translations.literal: Another method for computing lunar degree, the method says: multiply the new-moon small remainder by the minor circuit as dividend; multiply rule-years by the day factor as divisor; as the divisor yields one from the dividend, that is degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Alternate lunar-longitude method: set dividend = minor circuit × new-moon fractional day, divisor = rule-years × day factor; quotient gives degrees;

sentences.zh: 不滿法者，以章月除之為大分，餘為小分。

translations.literal: What does not fill the divisor, divide by rule-months to obtain large parts; the remainder is small parts.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder divides by 6,951 for large parts, with the tail as small parts.

sentences.zh: 所得以減合朔度及度分，算外，即所求年天正十一月朔夜半月所在度及分。

translations.literal: Subtract what is obtained from the syzygy degree and degree-parts; beyond the tally—and that is the degree and parts where the moon stands at midnight on the new moon of the celestial first month's eleventh month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract this from the syzygy longitude; one beyond the tally gives the midnight lunar position on the eleventh-month new moon.

sentences.zh: 求次月月度術[46]曰：月小，加度二十二、分七千三百七十三，月大，加度三十五、分一萬三千五百八十三，分滿日度法從度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即月次月所在度。

translations.literal: The method for finding the next month's lunar degree[46] says: for a short month, add twenty-two degrees and parts 7,373; for a long month, add thirty-five degrees and parts 13,583; when parts fill the day-degree factor, let them carry to degrees; remove by lodge sequence; what does not fill a lodge—beyond the tally—and that is the moon's degree in the next month.
translations.idiomatic: Next month's lunar longitude[46]: add 22° 7,373 parts for a short month or 35° 13,583 for a long month, carry through the day-degree factor, walk the lodges, and one beyond the tally marks the result.

sentences.zh: 求次日月度術[47]曰：加度十三、分六千二百一十，分滿日度法從度，除如上，算外，即月次日所在度。

translations.literal: The method for finding the next day's lunar degree[47] says: add thirteen degrees and parts 6,210; when parts fill the day-degree factor, let them carry to degrees; remove as above; beyond the tally—and that is the moon's degree on the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Next day's lunar longitude[47]: add 13° 6,210 parts, carry overflow, remove lodges as above; one beyond the tally is the result.

sentences.zh: 求弦望日所在度術曰：加合朔度七、大分六千四百五十一、小分三千四百六十七、[48]微分二，微分滿四從小分，小分滿章月從大分，大分滿日度法從度，命如上，算外，即上弦日所在度。

translations.literal: The method for finding the sun's degree at first and last quarter says: add to the syzygy degree seven, large fraction 6,451, small fraction 3,467, and[48] micro-fraction two; when micro-fractions fill four, let them carry to small parts; when small parts fill rule-months, let them carry to large parts; when large parts fill the day-degree factor, let them carry to degrees; assign as above; beyond the tally—and that is the sun's degree at first quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Solar longitude at first and last quarter: add 7°, 6,451 large parts, 3,467 small parts, and[48] 2 micro-parts to syzygy, carrying at 4, 6,951, and 16,860 respectively; count as above for first-quarter solar longitude.

sentences.zh: 又加，得望、[49]下弦、後月合朔。

translations.literal: Add again, and obtain full moon,[49] last quarter, and the next month's syzygy.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the addition for full moon,[49] last quarter, and the following syzygy.

sentences.zh: 求弦望月所在度術曰：加合朔度九十八、大分一萬一千六百九十五、小分五千二百二十五、微分一，滿除如上，算外，即上弦日月所在度。

translations.literal: The method for finding the moon's degree at first and last quarter says: add to the syzygy degree ninety-eight, large fraction 11,695, small fraction 5,225, and micro-fraction one; when full, remove as above; beyond the tally—and that is the shared degree of sun and moon at first quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar longitude at first and last quarter: add 98°, 11,695 large parts, 5,225 small parts, and 1 micro-part to syzygy, carry as above; one beyond the tally gives first-quarter lunar longitude.

sentences.zh: 又加，得望、下弦、後月合朔。

translations.literal: Add again, and obtain full moon, last quarter, and the next month's syzygy.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat for full moon, last quarter, and the following syzygy.

sentences.zh: 斗二十六度 牛八度 女十二度 虛十度

translations.literal: Dipper twenty-six degrees, Ox eight degrees, Woman twelve degrees, Void ten degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper 26°, Ox 8°, Maiden 12°, Emptiness 10°.

sentences.zh: 危十七度 室十六度 壁九度

translations.literal: Rooftop seventeen degrees, House sixteen degrees, Wall nine degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Rooftop 17°, House 16°, Wall 9°.

sentences.zh: 北方玄武七宿：九十八度分四千一百一十七

translations.literal: The seven lodges of the Northern Black Tortoise: ninety-eight degrees, parts four thousand one hundred seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Black Tortoise seven lodges: 98°, 4,117 parts.

sentences.zh: 奎十六度 婁十二度 胃十四度 昴十一度

translations.literal: Straddles sixteen degrees, Harvest twelve degrees, Stomach fourteen degrees, Hairy Head eleven degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Straddles 16°, Harvest 12°, Stomach 14°, Hairy Head 11°.

sentences.zh: 畢十六度 觜二度 參九度

translations.literal: Net sixteen degrees, Turtle Beak two degrees, Triaster nine degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Net 16°, Turtle Beak 2°, Triaster 9°.

sentences.zh: 西方白虎七宿：八十度

translations.literal: The seven lodges of the Western White Tiger: eighty degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Western White Tiger seven lodges: 80°.

sentences.zh: 井三十三度 鬼四度 柳十五度 星七度

translations.literal: Well thirty-three degrees, Ghost four degrees, Willow fifteen degrees, Star seven degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Well 33°, Ghost 4°, Willow 15°, Star 7°.

sentences.zh: 張十八度 翼十八度 軫十七度

translations.literal: Extended Net eighteen degrees, Wings eighteen degrees, Chariot Platform seventeen degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Extended Net 18°, Wings 18°, Chariot Platform 17°.

sentences.zh: 南方朱鳥七宿：一百一十二度

translations.literal: The seven lodges of the Southern Red Bird: one hundred twelve degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Red Bird seven lodges: 112°.

sentences.zh: 角十二度 亢九度 氐十五度 房五度

translations.literal: Horn twelve degrees, Gullet nine degrees, Base fifteen degrees, Chamber five degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Horn 12°, Gullet 9°, Base 15°, Chamber 5°.

sentences.zh: 心五度 尾十八度 箕十一度

translations.literal: Heart five degrees, Tail eighteen degrees, Winnowing Basket eleven degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Heart 5°, Tail 18°, Winnowing Basket 11°.

sentences.zh: 東方倉龍七宿：七十五度

translations.literal: The seven lodges of the Eastern Azure Dragon: seventy-five degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Azure Dragon seven lodges: 75°.

sentences.zh: 周天三百六十五度、一萬六千八百六十分度之四千一百一十七，通之，得六百一十五萬八千一十七，名曰周天。

translations.literal: The circuit of heaven: 365 degrees and 4,117 parts of one degree in 16,860 parts of a degree; communicating them, one obtains 6,158,017—and this is called the circuit of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The celestial circuit: 365° plus 4,117/16,860°; reduced to a common denominator, 6,158,017 parts—the value called the circuit of heaven.

sentences.zh: 推土王滅沒卦候上朔術第六

translations.literal: Method Six for computing Earth-sovereignty days, extinction and submergence, hexagram seasons, and superior syzygy.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure VI: Earth Sovereignty, Extinction/Submergence, Hexagram Seasons, and Superior Syzygy.

sentences.zh: 推土王日術曰：置四立大小餘，各減其大餘十八、小餘四千四百二十、小分十八、微分二，大餘不足減者，加六十乃減之；

translations.literal: The method for computing Earth-sovereignty days says: set the large and small remainders of the four establishings; from each subtract large remainder eighteen, small remainder 4,420, small parts eighteen, and micro-parts two; when the large remainder is insufficient to subtract, add sixty and then subtract;
translations.idiomatic: Earth-sovereignty day method: from each of the four establishing-term remainder lines subtract 18 large, 4,420 small, 18 small-part, and 2 micro-part units, borrowing 60 into the large remainder when needed;

sentences.zh: 小餘不足減者，減一日，加蔀法乃減之；

translations.literal: When the small remainder is insufficient to subtract, subtract one day, add the obscuration factor and then subtract;
translations.idiomatic: If the small remainder underflows, borrow one day and add the obscuration factor before subtracting;

sentences.zh: 小分不足減者，減小餘一，加小分法二十四乃減之；

translations.literal: When small parts are insufficient to subtract, subtract one from the small remainder, add the small-part factor twenty-four and then subtract;
translations.idiomatic: If small parts underflow, borrow one from the small remainder and add 24 (the small-part factor) before subtracting;

sentences.zh: 微分不足減者，減小分一，加五，然後皆減之。

translations.literal: When micro-parts are insufficient to subtract, subtract one from the small parts, add five, and then subtract all.
translations.idiomatic: If micro-parts underflow, borrow one small part and add 5 before completing the subtraction.

sentences.zh: 命以紀，算外，即四立前土王日。

translations.literal: Assign by era; beyond the tally—and that is the Earth-sovereignty day before the four establishings.
translations.idiomatic: Count from the era marker; one beyond the tally is the Earth-sovereignty day preceding an establishing term.

sentences.zh: 推土王又法，術曰：加冬至大餘二十七、小餘六千六百三十一、小分六、微分三，微分滿五從小分，小分滿小分法從小餘，小餘滿蔀法從大餘一，命以紀，算外，即季冬土王日。

translations.literal: Another method for computing Earth-sovereignty, the method says: add to the winter-solstice large remainder twenty-seven, small remainder 6,631, small parts six, and micro-parts three; when micro-parts fill five, let them carry to small parts; when small parts fill the small-part factor, let them carry to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the obscuration factor, let one carry to the large remainder; assign by era; beyond the tally—and that is the Earth-sovereignty day of late winter.
translations.idiomatic: Alternate Earth-sovereignty method: add 27, 6,631, 6, and 3 to the winter-solstice remainder stack, carrying at 5, 24, and the obscuration factor; count from the era marker for the late-winter Earth-sovereignty day.

sentences.zh: 求次季土王日術曰：加大餘九十一、小餘五千二百四十四、小分六，小分滿小分法從小餘，小餘滿蔀法從大餘，大餘滿六十去之，命以紀，算外，即次季土王日。

translations.literal: The method for finding the next season's Earth-sovereignty day says: add large remainder ninety-one, small remainder 5,244, and small parts six; when small parts fill the small-part factor, let them carry to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the obscuration factor, let it carry to the large remainder; when the large remainder fills sixty, remove it; assign by era; beyond the tally—and that is the next season's Earth-sovereignty day.
translations.idiomatic: Next season's Earth-sovereignty day: add 91, 5,244, and 6, carrying through the small-part and obscuration factors and casting out sexagenary cycles; count from the era marker.

sentences.zh: 推滅沒術曰：因冬至積沒有小餘者，加積沒一，以沒分乘之，以沒法八萬八千四百一十七除之，所得為積日，不盡為沒餘。

translations.literal: The method for computing extinction and submergence says: because the winter-solstice accumulated submergence has a small remainder, add one to the accumulated submergence; multiply by the submergence parts; divide by the submergence factor 88,417; what is obtained is accumulated days; what is not exhausted is the submergence remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Extinction/submergence method: if the winter-solstice accumulated submergence has a fractional tail, increment the count by one, multiply by the submergence parts, divide by 88,417 for accumulated days and submergence remainder.

sentences.zh: 六旬去積日，不盡為沒日，命以紀，算外，即所求天正十一月冬至後沒日。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated days; what is not exhausted is the submergence day; assign by era; beyond the tally—and that is the submergence day after the winter solstice of the celestial first month's eleventh month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Cast out sexagenary cycles from the accumulated days; the remainder is the submergence day; count from the era marker for the first submergence after the eleventh-month winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 求次滅術曰：加沒日六十九、沒餘五萬七千二百四十四，沒餘滿沒法從沒日，沒日滿六十去之，命以紀，算外，即次沒日。

translations.literal: The method for finding the next extinction says: add submergence day sixty-nine and submergence remainder 57,244; when the submergence remainder fills the submergence factor, let it carry to the submergence day; when the submergence day fills sixty, remove it; assign by era; beyond the tally—and that is the next submergence day.
translations.idiomatic: Next extinction day: add 69 days and 57,244 to the submergence remainder, carry through the submergence factor of 88,417, cast out sexagenary cycles, and count from the era marker.

sentences.zh: 餘盡者為滅。

translations.literal: When the remainder is exhausted, that is extinction.
translations.idiomatic: A zero remainder marks the extinction day.

sentences.zh: 求次沒術曰：加沒日六十九、沒餘一萬九百一十五、沒分六萬二千二百八十五，沒分滿沒法從沒餘，沒餘滿蔀法從沒日。

translations.literal: The method for finding the next submergence says: add submergence day sixty-nine, submergence remainder 10,915, and submergence parts 62,285; when submergence parts fill the submergence factor, let them carry to the submergence remainder; when the submergence remainder fills the obscuration factor, let it carry to the submergence day.
translations.idiomatic: Next submergence day: add 69 days, 10,915 remainder, and 62,285 parts, carrying through the submergence and obscuration factors.

sentences.zh: 命起前沒月，曆月大小除之，不滿月者，即後沒日及沒餘、沒分。

translations.literal: Assign starting from the prior submergence month; remove by long and short months of the calendar; what does not fill a month—and that is the later submergence day together with submergence remainder and submergence parts.
translations.idiomatic: Starting from the prior submergence month, divide by long and short months; the partial month yields the next submergence day, remainder, and parts.

sentences.zh: 命曰如上，算外，即次沒日。

translations.literal: Assign as above; beyond the tally—and that is the next submergence day.
translations.idiomatic: Count as above; one beyond the tally is the next submergence day.

sentences.zh: 推四正卦術曰：因冬至大小餘即坎卦用事日，春分即震卦用事日，夏至即離卦用事日，秋分即兌卦用事日。

translations.literal: The method for computing the four cardinal hexagrams says: following the winter-solstice large and small remainders—that is the day when the Kan hexagram takes effect; at the spring equinox, the day when the Zhen hexagram takes effect; at the summer solstice, the day when the Li hexagram takes effect; at the autumn equinox, the day when the Dui hexagram takes effect.
translations.idiomatic: Four cardinal hexagram method: the winter-solstice remainder line fixes Kan's governing day; spring equinox fixes Zhen; summer solstice fixes Li; autumn equinox fixes Dui.

sentences.zh: 中孚因坎卦。

translations.literal: Zhong Fu follows the Kan hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Fu derives from the Kan hexagram.

sentences.zh: 求次卦術曰：加坎卦大餘六，小餘一千四百七十三、小分十四、微分四，微分滿五從小分，小分滿小分法從小餘，小餘滿蔀法從大餘，大餘滿六十去之，命以紀，算外，即復卦用事日。

translations.literal: The method for finding the next hexagram says: add to the Kan hexagram large remainder six, small remainder 1,473, small parts fourteen, and micro-parts four; when micro-parts fill five, let them carry to small parts; when small parts fill the small-part factor, let them carry to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the obscuration factor, let it carry to the large remainder; when the large remainder fills sixty, remove it; assign by era; beyond the tally—and that is the day when the Fu hexagram takes effect.
translations.idiomatic: Next hexagram day: add 6, 1,473, 14, and 4 to the Kan line, carrying at 5, 24, and the obscuration factor and casting out sexagenary cycles; count from the era marker for Fu's governing day.

sentences.zh: 十一月，未濟、蹇、頤、中孚、復。

translations.literal: The eleventh month: Wei Ji, Jian, Yi, Zhong Fu, Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month hexagrams: Wei Ji, Jian, Yi, Zhong Fu, and Fu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，屯、謙、睽、升、臨。

translations.literal: The twelfth month: Tun, Qian, Kui, Sheng, Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month: Tun, Qian, Kui, Sheng, and Lin.

sentences.zh: 正月，小過、蒙、益、漸、泰。

translations.literal: The first month: Xiao Guo, Meng, Yi, Jian, Tai.
translations.idiomatic: First month: Xiao Guo, Meng, Yi, Jian, and Tai.

sentences.zh: 二月，需、隨、晉、解、大壯。

translations.literal: The second month: Xu, Sui, Jin, Xie, Da Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Second month: Xu, Sui, Jin, Xie, and Da Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 三月，豫、訟、蠱、革、夬。

translations.literal: The third month: Yu, Song, Gu, Ge, Guai.
translations.idiomatic: Third month: Yu, Song, Gu, Ge, and Guai.

sentences.zh: 四月，旅、師、比、小畜、乾。

translations.literal: The fourth month: Lü, Shi, Bi, Xiao Xu, Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month: Lü, Shi, Bi, Xiao Xu, and Qian.

sentences.zh: 五月，大有、家人、井、咸、姤。

translations.literal: The fifth month: Da You, Jia Ren, Jing, Xian, Gou.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month: Da You, Jia Ren, Jing, Xian, and Gou.

sentences.zh: 六月，鼎、豐、渙、履、遯。

translations.literal: The sixth month: Ding, Feng, Huan, Lü, Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: Ding, Feng, Huan, Lü, and Dun.

sentences.zh: 七月，恒、節、同人、損、否。

translations.literal: The seventh month: Heng, Jie, Tong Ren, Sun, Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: Heng, Jie, Tong Ren, Sun, and Pi.

sentences.zh: 八月，巽、萃、大畜、賁、觀。

translations.literal: The eighth month: Xun, Cui, Da Xu, Bi, Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: Xun, Cui, Da Xu, Bi, and Guan.

sentences.zh: 九月，歸妹、无妄、明夷、困、剝。

translations.literal: The ninth month: Gui Mei, Wu Wang, Ming Yi, Kun, Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Gui Mei, Wu Wang, Ming Yi, Kun, and Bo.

sentences.zh: 十月，艮、既濟、噬嗑、大過、坤。

translations.literal: The tenth month: Gen, Ji Ji, Shi He, Da Guo, Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month: Gen, Ji Ji, Shi He, Da Guo, and Kun.

sentences.zh: 四正為方伯，中孚為三公，復為天子，屯為諸侯，謙為大夫，睽為九卿，升還從三公，周而復始。

translations.literal: The four cardinals serve as regional lords; Zhong Fu as the Three Dukes; Fu as the Son of Heaven; Tun as feudal lords; Qian as grand masters; Kui as the nine ministers; Sheng returns and follows the Three Dukes—around and again from the start.
translations.idiomatic: The four cardinal hexagrams map to regional lords; Zhong Fu to the Three Dukes; Fu to the Son of Heaven; Tun to feudal lords; Qian to grand masters; Kui to the nine ministers; Sheng circles back to the Three Dukes—and the cycle repeats.

sentences.zh: 九三應上九，清淨、微溫、陽風；

translations.literal: When nine-three responds to upper nine: clear and pure, slightly warm, yang wind;
translations.idiomatic: Nine-three responding to upper nine brings clear skies, mild warmth, and yang wind;

sentences.zh: 九三應上六，降赤、决溫、陰雨。

translations.literal: When nine-three responds to upper six: descending red, decisive warmth, yin rain.
translations.idiomatic: Nine-three responding to upper six brings reddish haze, abrupt warmth, and yin rain.

sentences.zh: [50]六三應上六，日澤、寒、陰雨；

translations.literal: [50] When six-three responds to upper six: sun-bright damp, cold, yin rain;
translations.idiomatic: [50] Six-three responding to upper six brings bright dampness, cold, and overcast rain;

sentences.zh: [51]六三應上九，麴塵、決寒、陽風。

translations.literal: [51] When six-three responds to upper nine: flour dust, decisive cold, yang wind.
translations.idiomatic: [51] Six-three responding to upper nine brings dust haze, piercing cold, and yang wind.

sentences.zh: 諸卦上有陽爻者陽風，上有陰爻者陰雨。

translations.literal: Among hexagrams generally, those whose upper line is a yang line have yang wind; those whose upper line is a yin line have yin rain.
translations.idiomatic: For hexagrams generally: an upper yang line predicts yang wind; an upper yin line predicts yin rain.

sentences.zh: 推七十二候術曰：因冬至大小餘即虎始交日，加大餘五、小餘一千二百二十八、微分一，微分滿三從小分，小分滿小分法從小餘，小餘滿蔀法從大餘，大餘滿六十去之，命以紀，算外，依次候日。

translations.literal: The method for computing the seventy-two seasonal terms says: following the winter-solstice large and small remainders—that is the day when tigers begin mating; add large remainder five, small remainder 1,228, and micro-parts one; when micro-parts fill three, let them carry to small parts; when small parts fill the small-part factor, let them carry to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the obscuration factor, let it carry to the large remainder; when the large remainder fills sixty, remove it; assign by era; beyond the tally—and that is each successive seasonal-term day in order.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-two seasonal-term method: the winter-solstice remainder stack fixes the "tigers begin mating" day; add 5, 1,228, and 1 micro-part, carrying at 3, 24, and the obscuration factor and casting out sexagenary cycles; count from the era marker for each succeeding term day.

sentences.zh: 冬至 虎始交 芸始生 荔挺生

translations.literal: Winter solstice: tigers begin mating, rue begins sprouting, zhiting sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice terms: tigers begin mating; rue sprouts; zhiting sprouts.

sentences.zh: 小寒 蚯蚓結 麋角解 水泉動

translations.literal: Lesser cold: earthworms knot, elk antlers shed, spring waters stir.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser cold: earthworms coiled; elk shed antlers; springs flow.

sentences.zh: 大寒 雁北向 鵲始巢 雉始雊

translations.literal: Greater cold: wild geese turn north, magpies begin nesting, pheasants begin calling.
translations.idiomatic: Greater cold: geese head north; magpies nest; pheasants call.

sentences.zh: 立春 鷄始乳 東風解凍 蟄蟲始振

translations.literal: Establishment of spring: hens begin brooding, east wind melts ice, hibernating insects first stir.
translations.idiomatic: Start of spring: hens brood; east wind thaws ice; dormant insects awaken.

sentences.zh: 雨水 魚上負冰 獺祭魚 鴻雁來

translations.literal: Rain water: fish carry ice on their backs, otters offer fish, wild swans arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Rain water: fish surface under ice; otters "sacrifice" fish; swans return.

sentences.zh: 驚蟄 始雨水 桃始華 倉庚鳴

translations.literal: Awakening of insects: rain water begins, peach blossoms open, orioles call.
translations.idiomatic: Awakening of insects: rains begin; peaches bloom; orioles sing.

sentences.zh: 春分 鷹化為鳩 玄鳥至 雷始發聲

translations.literal: Spring equinox: hawks transform into cuckoos, dark birds arrive, thunder first sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Spring equinox: hawks turn to cuckoos; swallows arrive; thunder first rolls.

sentences.zh: 清明 電始見 蟄蟲咸動 蟄蟲啟戶

translations.literal: Clear brightness: lightning first appears, hibernating insects all stir, hibernating insects open their doors.
translations.idiomatic: Clear brightness: lightning appears; all dormant insects stir; insects emerge.

sentences.zh: 穀雨 桐始華 田鼠化為鴽 虹始見

translations.literal: Grain rain: paulownia first blooms, field mice transform into quail, rainbows first appear.
translations.idiomatic: Grain rain: paulownia blooms; field mice turn to quail; rainbows appear.

sentences.zh: 立夏 萍始生 戴勝降桑 螻蟈鳴

translations.literal: Establishment of summer: duckweed first sprouts, hoopoes alight on mulberry, mole crickets chirp.
translations.idiomatic: Start of summer: duckweed sprouts; hoopoes descend on mulberry; mole crickets chirp.

sentences.zh: 小滿 蚯蚓出 王瓜生 苦菜秀

translations.literal: Lesser fullness: earthworms emerge, serpent gourd grows, bitter greens flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser fullness: earthworms surface; serpent gourd grows; bitter greens flourish.

sentences.zh: 芒種 靡草死 小暑至 螗蜋生

translations.literal: Bearded grain: decadent grasses die, lesser heat arrives, mantises are born.
translations.idiomatic: Bearded grain: tender grasses die; lesser heat arrives; mantises hatch.

sentences.zh: 夏至 鵙始鳴 反舌無聲 鹿角解

translations.literal: Summer solstice: shrike first calls, mockingbirds fall silent, deer antlers shed.
translations.idiomatic: Summer solstice: shrike-cicadas call; mockingbirds fall silent; deer shed antlers.

sentences.zh: 小暑 蟬始鳴 半夏生 木槿榮

translations.literal: Lesser heat: cicadas first call, pinellia grows, hibiscus blooms.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser heat: cicadas sing; pinellia grows; hibiscus blooms.

sentences.zh: 大暑 溫風至 蟋蟀居壁 鷹乃學習

translations.literal: Greater heat: warm winds arrive, crickets dwell in walls, hawks learn to fly.
translations.idiomatic: Greater heat: warm winds blow; crickets move to walls; fledgling hawks practice flight.

sentences.zh: 立秋 腐草化為螢 土潤溽暑 涼風至

translations.literal: Establishment of autumn: rotting grass becomes fireflies, earth moist with lingering heat, cool winds arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Start of autumn: rotting grass becomes fireflies; earth damp with humid heat; cool winds blow.

sentences.zh: 處暑 白露降 寒蟬鳴 鷹祭鳥

translations.literal: End of heat: white dew descends, cold cicadas call, hawks "sacrifice" birds.
translations.idiomatic: End of heat: white dew falls; cold cicadas cry; hawks hunt birds.

sentences.zh: 白露 天地始肅 暴風至 鴻雁來

translations.literal: White dew: heaven and earth first grow stern, violent winds arrive, wild swans come.
translations.idiomatic: White dew: heaven and earth turn austere; storms rise; swans return.

sentences.zh: 秋分 玄鳥歸 羣鳥養羞 雷始收聲

translations.literal: Autumn equinox: dark birds return, flocking birds store provisions, thunder first withdraws its voice.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn equinox: swallows depart; birds hoard food; thunder fades.

sentences.zh: 寒露 蟄蟲附戶 殺氣浸盛 陽氣日衰

translations.literal: Cold dew: hibernating insects cling to doors, killing qi gradually surges, yang qi daily declines.
translations.idiomatic: Cold dew: insects shelter by doors; killing qi gathers; yang qi wanes day by day.

sentences.zh: 霜降 水始涸 鴻雁來賓 雀入大水化為蛤

translations.literal: Frost descends: waters first dry up, wild swans arrive as guests, sparrows enter great waters and transform into clams.
translations.idiomatic: Frost descends: waters shrink; swans arrive as guests; sparrows enter the waters and turn to clams.

sentences.zh: 立冬 菊有黃華 豺祭獸 水始冰

translations.literal: Establishment of winter: chrysanthemums show yellow blossoms, jackals "sacrifice" beasts, waters first freeze.
translations.idiomatic: Start of winter: chrysanthemums bloom yellow; jackals hunt game; waters begin to ice.

sentences.zh: 小雪 地始凍 雉入大水為蜃 虹藏不見

translations.literal: Lesser snow: earth first freezes, pheasants enter great waters and become clam-monsters, rainbows hide and are unseen.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser snow: earth freezes; pheasants enter the waters as shen-clams; rainbows vanish.

sentences.zh: 大雪 冰益壯 地始坼 鶡旦不鳴[52]

translations.literal: Greater snow: ice grows stronger, earth first splits, crossbills at dawn do not call[52].
translations.idiomatic: Greater snow: ice hardens; earth cracks; crossbills fall silent at dawn[52].

sentences.zh: 推上朔術曰：置入紀以來盡所求年，減一，以六律乘之，以六旬去之，不盡者命以甲子，算外，[53]即上朔日。

translations.literal: The method for computing the superior syzygy says: set the years elapsed since entering the era to the year sought, subtract one, multiply by the six pitch-pipes, remove by six decades; what is not exhausted assign from jiazi; beyond the tally—and [53] that is the superior syzygy day.
translations.idiomatic: Superior syzygy method: take years since era entry for the year sought, subtract 1, multiply by 6, cast out sexagenary cycles, count from jiazi; one beyond the tally[53] is the superior syzygy day.

sentences.zh: 推五星見伏術第七

translations.literal: Method Seven for computing the five stars' appearance and hiding.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure VII: Five Stars, Appearance and Occultation.

sentences.zh: 上元甲子以來至今大魏興和二年，歲在庚申，積二十九萬三千九百九十七算。

translations.literal: From the upper origin jiazi to the present, Great Wei's Xinghe year 2, the year stationed in gengshen, accumulated 293,997 tallies.
translations.idiomatic: From the upper origin in a jiazi year to the present—Great Wei's Xinghe year 2, a gengshen year—the accumulated count is 293,997.

sentences.zh: 木精曰歲星，其數六百七十二萬三千八百八十八。

translations.literal: The essence of wood is called the Year Star; its number is 6,723,888.
translations.idiomatic: Wood's essence is Jupiter; its divisor is 6,723,888.

sentences.zh: 火精曰熒惑，其數一千三百一十四萬九千八十三。

translations.literal: The essence of fire is called the Sparkling Deluder; its number is 13,149,083.
translations.idiomatic: Fire's essence is Mars; its divisor is 13,149,083.

sentences.zh: 土精曰鎮星，其數六百三十七萬四千六十一。

translations.literal: The essence of earth is called the Quelling Star; its number is 6,374,061.
translations.idiomatic: Earth's essence is Saturn; its divisor is 6,374,061.

sentences.zh: 金精曰太白，其數九百八十四萬三千八百八十二。

translations.literal: The essence of metal is called Great White; its number is 9,843,882.
translations.idiomatic: Metal's essence is Venus; its divisor is 9,843,882.

sentences.zh: 水精曰辰星，其數一百九十五萬三千七百一十六。

translations.literal: The essence of water is called the Chronogram Star; its number is 1,953,716.
translations.idiomatic: Water's essence is Mercury; its divisor is 1,953,716.

translations.literal: [Editorial note 54.]
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note 54.

sentences.zh: 推五星術曰：置上元以來盡所求年，減一，以周天乘之，為五星之實；

translations.literal: The method for computing the five stars says: set the years from the upper origin to the year sought, subtract one, multiply by the circuit of heaven—this is the five stars' dividend;
translations.idiomatic: Five-star method: take years from the upper origin to the year sought, subtract 1, multiply by the celestial circuit for the five-star dividend;

sentences.zh: 各以其數為法，除之，所得為積合，不盡為合餘。

translations.literal: each taking its own number as divisor, divide; what is obtained is accumulated conjunction; what is not exhausted is conjunction remainder.
translations.idiomatic: divide each by its planet's divisor for accumulated conjunction and conjunction remainder.

sentences.zh: 以合餘減法，餘為入歲度分。

translations.literal: Subtract the conjunction remainder from the divisor; the remainder is entry into the year's degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the conjunction remainder from the divisor for the year's degree-fraction.

sentences.zh: 以日度法約之，所得即所求年天正十一月冬至後晨夕合度算及度餘。

translations.literal: Reduce by the day-degree factor; what is obtained is the morning-and-evening conjunction degree-tally and degree-remainder after the winter solstice of the celestial first month's eleventh month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce by the day-degree factor for the morning/evening conjunction degree count and remainder after the eleventh-month winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 其金、水，以一合日數及合餘減合度算及度餘，得一者為晨，無所得者為夕；

translations.literal: For metal and water, subtract one conjunction-day count and conjunction remainder from the conjunction-degree tally and degree-remainder; where one is obtained, that is morning; where nothing is obtained, that is evening;
translations.idiomatic: For Venus and Mercury, subtract one conjunction-day count and remainder from the degree tally; a result of 1 means morning, 0 means evening;

sentences.zh: 若度餘不足減者，減合度算一，加日度法乃減之。

translations.literal: if the degree-remainder is insufficient to subtract, subtract one from the conjunction-degree tally, add the day-degree factor and then subtract.
translations.idiomatic: If the degree remainder underflows, borrow 1 from the degree tally and add the day-degree factor before subtracting.

sentences.zh: 命起牛前十二度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即所求年天正十一月冬至後晨夕合度及度餘。

translations.literal: Assign starting twelve degrees before Ox; remove by lodge sequence; what does not fill a lodge—and beyond the tally that is the morning-and-evening conjunction degree and degree-remainder after the winter solstice of the celestial first month's eleventh month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Count from 12° before Ox, walk the lodges; the partial lodge yields the morning/evening conjunction longitude and remainder after the eleventh-month winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 徑推五星術曰：置上元以來盡所求年，減一，如法算之。

translations.literal: The direct method for computing the five stars says: set the years from the upper origin to the year sought, subtract one, compute by the divisor method.
translations.idiomatic: Direct five-star method: take years from the upper origin to the year sought, subtract 1, and compute by each planet's divisor.

sentences.zh: 合度餘滿日度法，加合度算一，合度算滿合終日數去之。

translations.literal: When conjunction degree-remainder fills the day-degree factor, add one to the conjunction-degree tally; when the conjunction-degree tally fills the total conjunction-day count, remove it.
translations.idiomatic: Carry conjunction degree-remainder overflow into the degree tally; when the tally fills the planet's total conjunction-day count, cast it out.

sentences.zh: 亦以合終日餘減合度餘，[55]若不足減者，減合度算一，加周虛。

translations.literal: Also subtract the total conjunction-day remainder from the conjunction degree-remainder; [55] if insufficient to subtract, subtract one from the conjunction-degree tally and add cycle void.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the total conjunction-day remainder from the degree remainder;[55] if underflow occurs, borrow 1 from the degree tally and add cycle void.

sentences.zh: [56]所得即所求年天正十一月冬至後晨夕合度算及度餘。

translations.literal: [56] What is obtained is the morning-and-evening conjunction degree-tally and degree-remainder after the winter solstice of the celestial first month's eleventh month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: [56] The result is the morning/evening conjunction degree count and remainder after the eleventh-month winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 其求金水及命度，[57]皆如上法。

translations.literal: The computation for metal and water and assigning the degree, [57] all follow the method above.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Venus, Mercury, and their assigned longitudes[57] all follow the method above.

sentences.zh: 求星合月及日術曰：置冬至去朔日數，減一，加合度算。

translations.literal: The method for finding the star's conjunction month and day says: set the count of days from the winter solstice to new moon, subtract one, add the conjunction-degree tally.
translations.idiomatic: Star conjunction month and day: set days from winter solstice to new moon, subtract 1, add the conjunction-degree tally.

sentences.zh: 冬至小餘以加合度餘，合度餘滿日度法去之，加合度算一。

translations.literal: Add the winter-solstice small remainder to the conjunction degree-remainder; when the conjunction degree-remainder fills the day-degree factor, remove it and add one to the conjunction-degree tally.
translations.idiomatic: Add the winter-solstice fractional day to the degree remainder, carry overflow into the degree tally.

translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 置差令朔 「令朔」不可解，疑「令」乃「合」之訛。

translations.literal: Set discrepancies to align the new moon — "align new moon" is unintelligible; suspect "令" is an error for "合".
translations.idiomatic: "Set discrepancies to align the new moon": "align new moon" is unintelligible; "令" is probably a corruption of "合" (conjunction).

sentences.zh: 新曆歲星在營室十三度 諸本「新曆」下脫「歲星」兩字，依下文鎮星、太白例補。

translations.literal: The new calendar has the Year Star in Encampment Room at thirteen degrees — all editions omit the two characters "Year Star" after "new calendar"; supplied per the Saturn and Venus examples below.
translations.idiomatic: "New calendar, Year Star in Encampment Room at 13°": all editions omit 歲星 after 新曆; restored following the Saturn and Venus entries below.

sentences.zh: 十蔀成紀 諸本「十」作「千」。

translations.literal: Ten obscurations form an era-cycle — all editions read "thousand" for "ten".
translations.idiomatic: "Ten obscurations form an era-cycle": all editions read 千 for 十.

sentences.zh: 按蔀法一萬六千八百六十，十蔀成十六萬八千六百，正為一紀之數。

translations.literal: By the obscuration factor 16,860, ten obscurations yield 168,600 — exactly the number for one era-cycle.
translations.idiomatic: The obscuration factor is 16,860; ten obscurations yield 168,600—the count of one era-cycle.

sentences.zh: 「千」顯誤，今改正。

translations.literal: "Thousand" is clearly erroneous; corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: "Thousand" is clearly wrong; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 十二分度法 諸本「十」作「小」。

translations.literal: Twelve-part degree method — all editions read "small" for "ten".
translations.idiomatic: "Twelve-part degree method": all editions read 小 for 十.

sentences.zh: 按以十二除度法一萬六千八百六十，得一千四百五，乃為一氣時法之數。

translations.literal: Dividing the degree factor 16,860 by twelve yields 1,405 — the number for one qi-term time factor.
translations.idiomatic: Dividing the degree factor 16,860 by 12 yields 1,405—the qi-term time factor.

sentences.zh: 「小」係形近致誤，今改正。

translations.literal: "Small" arose from graphic similarity; corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: "Small" is a graphic corruption; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 二十九章十一年減閏餘一一萬六百七十八年減一閏月 諸本「閏餘一，一」作「閏餘二」，「六百」作「一百」，「減」下有「右」字。

translations.literal: Twenty-nine rules and eleven years reduce the intercalation remainder by one — 10,678 years reduce one intercalary month — all editions read "intercalation remainder two" for "intercalation remainder one, one", "one hundred" for "six hundred", and add "right" below "reduce".
translations.idiomatic: "Twenty-nine rules and eleven years reduce the intercalation remainder by one; 10,678 years reduce one intercalary month": all editions read 閏餘二 for 閏餘一，一, 一百 for 六百, and add 右 after 減.

sentences.zh: 按興和曆一章歲等於古法

translations.literal: By the Xinghe calendar, one rule-year equals the ancient method
translations.idiomatic: By the Xinghe calendar, one rule-year equals that of the ancient method

sentences.zh: (十九年一章)

translations.literal: (nineteen years per rule)
translations.idiomatic: (nineteen years per rule)

sentences.zh: 之二十九章加十一年，而閏餘減一；

translations.literal: — twenty-nine rules plus eleven years, and the intercalation remainder decreases by one;
translations.idiomatic: — twenty-nine rules plus eleven years, with the intercalation remainder reduced by one;

sentences.zh: 積十九章歲，即一萬六百七十八年則減一閏月。

translations.literal: accumulating nineteen rule-years, that is 10,678 years, then one intercalary month is subtracted.
translations.idiomatic: after nineteen accumulated rule-years—that is, 10,678 years—one intercalary month is subtracted.

sentences.zh: 傳本將「閏餘一，一萬」之兩「一」字誤并成「二」字，「六百」誤為「一百」，又衍「右」字，今俱改正。

translations.literal: The transmitted text erroneously merged the two "one" characters in "intercalation remainder one, ten thousand" into "two", changed "six hundred" to "one hundred", and added a spurious "right"; all corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: The transmitted text merged the two 一 in 閏餘一，一萬 into 二, changed 六百 to 一百, and added a spurious 右; all corrected here.

sentences.zh: 閏月數 諸本「閏」訛「間」，今依文義改。

translations.literal: Intercalary month count — all editions have "interval" for "intercalary"; corrected per the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: "Intercalary month count": all editions read 間 for 閏; corrected per context.

sentences.zh: 內分五萬七千二百四十四 諸本「二百四十四」作「一百八十四」。

translations.literal: Inner parts 57,244 — all editions read "one hundred eighty-four" for "two hundred forty-four".
translations.idiomatic: "Inner parts 57,244": all editions read 一百八十四 for 二百四十四.

sentences.zh: 按以沒法八萬八千四百一十七除沒分六百一十五萬八千一十七，得經沒六十九、分五萬二百四十四。

translations.literal: Dividing extinction part 6,158,017 by extinction factor 88,417 yields sixty-nine extinction cycles and remainder 50,244.
translations.idiomatic: Dividing the extinction part 6,158,017 by the extinction factor 88,417 yields 69 extinction cycles and remainder 50,244.

sentences.zh: 數字顯誤，今改正。

translations.literal: The numeral is clearly wrong; corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: The numeral is clearly wrong; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 五月二十三分月之二十也 諸本「五月」作「周髀六」。

translations.literal: "May — twenty-three parts of the month's twenty" — all editions read "Zhou Bi six" for "May".
translations.idiomatic: "May, twenty-three parts of the month's twenty": all editions read 周髀六 for 五月.

sentences.zh: 按會數為五月二十三分月之二十的整日數，「周髀六」三字當衍，又脫「五月」兩字。

translations.literal: The conjunction number is the whole-day count of "May, twenty-three parts of the month's twenty"; the three characters "Zhou Bi six" are interpolations, and "May" is omitted.
translations.idiomatic: The conjunction number is the whole-day count of "May, 23/20 of a month"; 周髀六 is an interpolation and 五月 is missing.

sentences.zh: 今改正。

translations.literal: Corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected here.

sentences.zh: 百七十三日 諸本「三」作「二」。

translations.literal: One hundred seventy-three days — all editions read "two" for "three".
translations.idiomatic: "173 days": all editions read 二 for 三.

sentences.zh: 按此數即上會數，「二」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: This number is the conjunction number above; "two" is erroneous; corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: This is the conjunction number above; 二 is wrong; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 百七十三 諸本「三」作「二」。

translations.literal: One hundred seventy-three — all editions read "two" for "three".
translations.idiomatic: "173": all editions read 二 for 三.

sentences.zh: 按此數亦即上會數，「二」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: This number is also the conjunction number above; "two" is erroneous; corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: This is likewise the conjunction number above; 二 is wrong; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 周天用一日月行數除 諸本「日」上脫「一」字，「數」下脫「除」字。

translations.literal: Circuit of heaven divided by one day's moon-motion count — all editions omit "one" before "day" and "divide" after "count".
translations.idiomatic: "Circuit of heaven divided by one day's moon-motion count": all editions omit 一 before 日 and 除 after 數.

sentences.zh: 按周日為小周

translations.literal: By the circuit remainder — the lesser circuit
translations.idiomatic: The circuit remainder is the lesser circuit

sentences.zh: (即一日月行數)

translations.literal: (that is, one day's moon-motion count)
translations.idiomatic: (that is, one day's moon-motion count)

sentences.zh: 除周天所得之整數。

translations.literal: The whole number obtained by dividing the circuit of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: the whole number obtained by dividing the circuit of heaven.

sentences.zh: 原文脫漏，今補。

translations.literal: The original text is defective; supplied here.
translations.idiomatic: The original text is defective; supplied here.

sentences.zh: 周餘 諸本「周」訛「用」，今依文義改正。

translations.literal: Circuit remainder — all editions have "use" for "circuit"; corrected per the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: "Circuit remainder": all editions read 用 for 周; corrected per context.

sentences.zh: 減半月小餘之外 按入交限數為會通減通數之半，除以日法，即得一百五十八度。

translations.literal: Beyond subtracting half the lunation's small remainder — the entry-into-crossing limit is conjunction common minus half the common number, divided by the day factor, yielding one hundred fifty-eight degrees.
translations.idiomatic: "Beyond subtracting half the lunation's small remainder": the entry-into-crossing limit is half of (conjunction common minus common number), divided by the day factor, yielding 158°.

sentences.zh: 其餘數為十一萬六千五十八半。

translations.literal: The remaining number is 116,058.5.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining number is 116,058.5.

sentences.zh: 此注或由錯簡，致與正文迥無關係，依術當作「一百五十八度外不成度之數」。

translations.literal: This note may have been misplaced by faulty binding, bearing no relation to the main text; per the method it should read "the number of incomplete degrees outside one hundred fifty-eight degrees."
translations.idiomatic: This note may be a misbound interpolation unrelated to the main text; per the method it should read "the fractional degrees outside 158°."

sentences.zh: 命以紀算外 諸本「算」下脫「外」字，今依文義補。

translations.literal: Assign beyond the era tally — all editions omit "beyond" after "tally"; supplied per the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: "Assign beyond the era tally": all editions omit 外 after 算; supplied per context.

sentences.zh: 命如上 諸本「上」訛「止」，今依文義改正。

translations.literal: Assign as above — all editions have "stop" for "above"; corrected per the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: "Assign as above": all editions read 止 for 上; corrected per context.

sentences.zh: 閏月有進退 諸本「退」訛「即」，今依文義改正。

translations.literal: Intercalary months have advance and retreat — all editions have "then" for "retreat"; corrected per the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: "Intercalary months have advance and retreat": all editions read 即 for 退; corrected per context.

sentences.zh: 如章閏得一 諸本「如」訛「加」，今依文義改正。

translations.literal: When the rule intercalation yields one — all editions have "add" for "as"; corrected per the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: "When the rule intercalation yields one": all editions read 加 for 如; corrected per context.

sentences.zh: 度餘三萬九千三百三十九 諸本「三十九」作「四十九」。

translations.literal: Degree remainder 39,339 — all editions read "forty-nine" for "thirty-nine".
translations.idiomatic: "Degree remainder 39,339": all editions read 四十九 for 三十九.

sentences.zh: 按甲戌紀交會差二千六百五十二萬二千六百四十九除以日法二十萬八千五百三十，得交會差一百二十七度、度餘三萬九千三百三十九。

translations.literal: Dividing the jiaxu-era conjunction discrepancy 26,522,649 by the day factor 208,530 yields conjunction discrepancy 127 degrees and degree remainder 39,339.
translations.idiomatic: Dividing the jiaxu-era conjunction discrepancy 26,522,649 by the day factor 208,530 yields a conjunction discrepancy of 127° with remainder 39,339.

sentences.zh: 「四十」乃「三十」之訛，今改正。

translations.literal: "Forty" is an error for "thirty"; corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: "Forty" is a corruption of "thirty"; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 算外 諸本「算」下脫「外」字，今依文義補。

translations.literal: Beyond the tally — all editions omit "beyond" after "tally"; supplied per the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: "Beyond the tally": all editions omit 外 after 算; supplied per context.

sentences.zh: 其月朔則交會 諸本「會」訛「道」，今依文義改正。

translations.literal: That month's new moon then crosses in conjunction — all editions have "path" for "conjunction"; corrected per the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: "That month's new moon then crosses in conjunction": all editions read 道 for 會; corrected per context.

sentences.zh: 即是不蝕度 諸本「蝕」訛「餘」，今依文義改正。

translations.literal: That is the non-eclipse degree — all editions have "remainder" for "eclipse"; corrected per the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: "That is the non-eclipse degree": all editions read 餘 for 蝕; corrected per context.

sentences.zh: 餘為蝕分 諸本「為」下衍「餘」字，今依文義刪。

translations.literal: The remainder is the eclipse fraction — all editions have a spurious "remainder" after "is"; deleted per the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: "The remainder is the eclipse fraction": all editions add a spurious 餘 after 為; deleted per context.

sentences.zh: 甲戌紀遲差分二百三十五萬二千一百九十一 諸本「二百」作「二日」，「二千」作「三千」。

translations.literal: Jiaxu-era slow-discrepancy parts 2,352,191 — all editions read "two days" for "two hundred" and "three thousand" for "two thousand".
translations.idiomatic: "Jiaxu-era slow-discrepancy parts 2,352,191": all editions read 二日 for 二百 and 三千 for 二千.

sentences.zh: 按以一紀月數二百八萬五千三百乘通數六百一十五萬八千一十七，以通周五百七十四萬五千九百四十一去之，得甲戌紀遲差分二百三十五萬二千一百九十一。

translations.literal: Multiplying one era-cycle's month count 2,085,300 by the common number 6,158,017 and removing the common circuit 5,745,941 yields jiaxu-era slow-discrepancy parts 2,352,191.
translations.idiomatic: Multiplying one era-cycle's month count 2,085,300 by the common number 6,158,017 and subtracting the common circuit 5,745,941 yields jiaxu-era slow-discrepancy parts 2,352,191.

sentences.zh: 知「日」乃「百」之訛，「三千」乃「二千」之訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Recognizing "day" is an error for "hundred" and "three thousand" for "two thousand"; corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: Recognizing 日 as a corruption of 百 and 三千 of 二千; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 所得為積周 諸本「為積周」訛「日餘周」，今依正光曆例改正。

translations.literal: What is obtained is accumulated circuits — all editions have "day-remainder circuits" for "is accumulated circuits"; corrected per the Zhengguang calendar example.
translations.idiomatic: "What is obtained is accumulated circuits": all editions read 日餘周 for 為積周; corrected per the Zhengguang calendar.

sentences.zh: 日蝕滿日法從日 諸本「日法從日」誤倒作「日從日法」，今依文義乙正。

translations.literal: When the eclipse fills the day factor, carry to days — all editions invert "day factor carry to days" as "days carry to day factor"; reordered per the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: "When the eclipse fills the day factor, carry to days": all editions invert 日法從日 as 日從日法; reordered per context.

sentences.zh: 月行遲疾度及分 諸本「分」訛「合」，今依文義改正。

translations.literal: Moon's slow and fast motion degrees and parts — all editions have "conjunction" for "parts"; corrected per the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: "Moon's slow and fast motion degrees and parts": all editions read 合 for 分; corrected per context.

sentences.zh: 十四度

translations.literal: Fourteen degrees.

sentences.zh: 〈三百三十四分〉

translations.literal: 〈Three hundred thirty-four parts.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈334 parts.〉

sentences.zh: 諸本「三十四分」作「三十十四分」，衍一「十」字。

translations.literal: All editions read "thirty-fourteen parts" for "thirty-four parts" — one spurious "ten".
translations.idiomatic: All editions read 三十十四分 for 三十四分—one spurious 十.

sentences.zh: 按本表各項數字，今依下列方法加以校算：

translations.literal: The numbers in this table are now rechecked by the following methods:
translations.idiomatic: The figures in this table are now rechecked by the following methods:

translations.literal: (one)

sentences.zh: 月行遲疾度及分：以月日平行分七千五百一十三

translations.literal: Moon's slow and fast motion degrees and parts: using the moon-sun mean motion parts 7,513
translations.idiomatic: Moon slow/fast degrees and parts: using the moon-sun mean motion parts 7,513

sentences.zh: (即小周)

translations.literal: (that is, the lesser circuit)
translations.idiomatic: (that is, the lesser circuit)

sentences.zh: 加減本日損益率

translations.literal: add or subtract this day's increase-decrease rate
translations.idiomatic: add or subtract this day's correction rate

sentences.zh: (損減、益加)

translations.literal: (for decrease subtract, for increase add)
translations.idiomatic: (subtract for 損, add for 益)

sentences.zh: ，以章歲五百六十二約之為度，餘為分。

translations.literal: , reduce by rule-years 562 to make degrees; the remainder is parts.
translations.idiomatic: , divide by the rule-years constant of 562 to obtain degrees; the remainder is the fractional parts.

translations.literal: (two)

sentences.zh: 損益率：以各日月實行度分化為分，減以月日平行分七千五百一十三即得。

translations.literal: Increase-decrease rate: convert each day's sun-moon actual motion degree-parts into parts, subtract the moon-sun mean motion parts 7,513, and that is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Correction rate: convert each tabulated sun-moon actual motion value into parts, subtract the mean motion parts of 7,513, and the result is the rate.

translations.literal: (three)

sentences.zh: 盈縮并率：將本日前各日損益率累加得之。

translations.literal: Excess-shortage combined rate: obtained by cumulatively adding each day's increase-decrease rates before this day.
translations.idiomatic: Combined excess/shortage rate: sum all correction rates from preceding days through the current day.

translations.literal: (four)

sentences.zh: 盈縮積分：盈縮并率乘日法二十萬八千五百三十，約以小周七千五百一十三，即得。

translations.literal: Excess-shortage accumulated parts: multiply the excess-shortage combined rate by the day factor 208,530, reduce by the lesser circuit 7,513, and that is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated excess/shortage parts: multiply the combined rate by the day factor of 208,530, then divide by the lesser circuit of 7,513.

sentences.zh: 以下至校勘記[三七]，逕指出傳本譌誤所在，校改理由不再贅述。

translations.literal: From here to collation note [37], we directly indicate where the transmitted text errs; the rationale for each emendation will not be repeated.
translations.idiomatic: From here through collation note [37], each entry simply marks the error in the transmitted text; detailed arguments for the emendations are omitted.

sentences.zh: 盈七百五十七 諸本「十」下脫「七」字，今據校算補。

translations.literal: Excess 757 — all editions omit the character "seven" below "ten"; now supplied per collation calculation.
translations.idiomatic: "Excess 757": all editions omit 七 after 十; supplied per recalculation.

sentences.zh: 二百六十一分 諸本「二百」下衍「四十」兩字，今據校算刪。

translations.literal: Two hundred sixty-one parts — all editions have a spurious "forty" after "two hundred"; now deleted per collation calculation.
translations.idiomatic: "261 parts": all editions add spurious 四十 after 二百; deleted per recalculation.

translations.literal: Increase 616 — all editions have "seventeen" for "sixteen"; corrected per collation calculation.
translations.idiomatic: "Increase 616": all editions read 十七 for 十六; corrected per recalculation.

sentences.zh: 盈一千四百四十六 諸本「四十六」訛「三十六」，今據校算改正。

translations.idiomatic: "Excess 1,446": all editions read 三十六 for 四十六; corrected per recalculation.

translations.idiomatic: "267 parts": all editions read 三百 for 二百; corrected per recalculation.

translations.literal: Increase 646 — all editions have "thirty-six" for "forty-six"; corrected per collation calculation.
translations.idiomatic: "Increase 646": all editions read 三十六 for 四十六; corrected per recalculation.

translations.literal: Three hundred twenty-four parts — all editions have "two hundred" for "three hundred"; corrected per collation calculation.
translations.idiomatic: "324 parts": all editions read 二百 for 三百; corrected per recalculation.
